name: Cadillac Mountain
summary: The highest headland on the eastern seaboard, and among the first places in the United States to catch the sunrise.

name: Jordan Pond
summary: A glacial tarn below the twin summits of the Bubbles, circled by a level shore path.

name: Thunder Hole
summary: A narrow inlet where an incoming swell slams air out of a sea cave with a boom.

name: Sand Beach
summary: A pocket of shell sand between granite headlands, in water that rarely passes 55°F.

name: Otter Cliff
summary: A 110-foot granite wall dropping straight into the Atlantic.

name: Bass Harbor Head Light
summary: An 1858 light station on the island's quiet south-western shore.

name: Schoodic Point
summary: The park's mainland section, where dark basalt dykes cut through pink granite ledges.

image.caption: schoodic point
image.altText: Two women walking on a rocky shore with water and a mountain the backgound

name: Park Loop Road
summary: Twenty-seven miles threading the eastern side of Mount Desert Island, designed to reveal the coast a view at a time.

name: Acadia Gateway Center
summary: The Acadia Gateway Center is an intermodal transit and welcome center located on Route 3 in Trenton three miles north of Mount Desert Island. Facilities include an Island Explorer bus stop, day-use parking, and an 11,000-square-foot welcome center with tourism information, a store, waiting area, and restrooms.
hours: 8 am to 6 pm, Wed May 20 to Mon Oct 12, 2026

name: Hulls Cove Visitor Center
summary: Located close to Bar Harbor off Route 3, the Hulls Cove Visitor Center is Acadia’s main visitor contact station and transportation hub from May into October. It is a popular, and often crowded, first stop for many visitors.

name: Islesford Historical Museum
summary: The Islesford Historical Museum continues its mission of celebrating Islesford’s cultural history. Historical exhibits showcase life on and around Cranberry Isles from the 1700s to present.

name: Schoodic Institute Welcome Center at Rockefeller Hall
summary: The Schoodic Institute Welcome Center at Rockefeller Hall is located on Schoodic Peninsula off the one-way loop road. Exhibits about the old Navy base and park information can be found here.

name: Sieur de Monts Nature Center
summary: Sieur de Monts Nature Center has visitor services, hiking information, and interactive exhibits. It acts as a trailhead for many hiking trails starting in the Sieur de Monts area.

name: Winter Information: Bar Harbor Chamber of Commerce
summary: During winter and spring, information and sales of some passes are available at the Bar Harbor Chamber of Commerce, 2 Cottage Street, at the corner of Cottage and Main streets (GPS coordinates = 44.398633, -68.204933). The center is open 7 days a week from 8 am to 4 pm.

name: Blackwoods Campground
summary: Blackwoods Campground is located on the east side of Mount Desert Island, about 5 miles (8 km) south of Bar Harbor on Route 3.

name: Seawall Campground
summary: Seawall Campground is located on the west side of Mount Desert Island about 4 miles (6 km) south of Southwest Harbor.

name: Schoodic Woods Campground
summary: Schoodic Woods Campground is the newest campground in the park and located 1.5 miles (2.5 km) southeast of Winter Harbor on the Schoodic Peninsula.

name: Duck Harbor Campground
summary: Duck Harbor Campground is located on Isle au Haut, a rugged island off the coast of Stonington, Maine.

name: Mount Alava
summary: The ridge-top trail above Pago Pago Harbor, with the harbor on one side and the north coast falling away on the other.

image.caption: Mount Alava
image.altText: A lush group of mountains surrounded by ocean with a lakeside town nested in the mountain valley.

name: Vatia and Pola Island
summary: A north-coast village beneath the ridge, facing the sheer sea stack of Pola Island.

name: Ofu Beach
summary: A long white-sand beach on Ofu, with some of the clearest snorkelling in the territory over the reef.

name: Saua
summary: A site on Taʻū that Samoan tradition holds sacred, below forested cliffs.

image.caption: Sau well
image.altText: A close up picture of a well in the ground surrounded by mossy rocks.

name: Visitor Center and Park Store
summary: Open on weekdays from 8:00 am to 3:00 pm. Closed on weekends and federal holidays.
hours: Offering essential information, interactive exhibits, and a chance to learn about the park’s unique cultural and natural heritage, the visitor center provides an introduction to everything that makes this park special.

name: Delicate Arch
summary: The free-standing arch on Utah's licence plates, reached by a three-mile round trip across open slickrock — or seen from below at the viewpoints.

image.caption: Wolfe Ranch Trailhead and Parking Lot
image.altText: Visitors read the Delicate Arch Trailhead panel before embarking on a hike.

name: Landscape Arch
summary: The longest arch in the park, a thin ribbon of rock along the Devils Garden trail.

image.caption: Devils Garden Trailhead
image.altText: Hikers reading a trailhead sign near a fence, sandstone walls in background

name: The Windows
summary: North and South Window and Turret Arch, a short loop from the parking area.

image.caption: North Window
image.altText: rock steps lead to an orange stone arch towering over a tiny person standing beneath it

name: Double Arch
summary: Two arches sharing one end, a short walk from the Windows.

image.caption: Double Arch
image.altText: Two sandstone arches connected on the left against a backdrop of blue sky.

name: Balanced Rock
summary: A boulder the size of three school buses on a slender pedestal, right beside the road.

image.caption: Balanced Rock at sunset
image.altText: Sandstone boulder atop a its pedestal glows bright orange at sunset, snowy peaks in background

name: Park Avenue
summary: A canyon walled by fins and monoliths, the first big view inside the park.

image.caption: Park Avenue Viewpoint
image.altText: Sandstone spires seen in the distance from Park Avenue Viewpoint

name: Fiery Furnace
summary: A maze of narrow sandstone fins, entered only on a ranger-led hike or with a permit.

image.caption: Fiery Furnace Overlook
image.altText: Fiery Furnace Overlook

name: Wolfe Ranch
summary: A homesteader's cabin from the turn of the twentieth century, with Ute rock art nearby, at the start of the Delicate Arch trail.

image.caption: Wolfe Ranch Cabin
image.altText: wooden cabin structure with a door surrounded by a wooden fence and shrubs

name: Arches Visitor Center
summary: The visitor center is generally open every day except December 25. Hours vary by season.

name: Devils Garden Campground
summary: Camp among slickrock outcroppings at Devils Garden Campground, 18 miles from the park entrance.

name: Notch Trail
summary: A canyon walk and a log ladder up to a notch with a view over the White River valley.

image.caption: Notch Trail
image.altText: A sign marked Notch Trail alongside a trail proceeding amid badlands buttes under blue sky.

name: Door Trail
summary: A short boardwalk through a break in the Badlands Wall into a maze of eroded formations.

image.caption: Door Trail
image.altText: A sign marked Door Trail next to blue ADA sign with badlands buttes and boardwalk under blue sky.

name: Fossil Exhibit Trail
summary: A boardwalk with casts of the fossils found in the park, beside the formations they came from.

image.caption: Fossil Exhibit Trail
image.altText: A boardwalk extends towards badlands formations under blue sky amid exhibit and rattlesnake sign.

name: Yellow Mounds Overlook
summary: Rounded hills of bright yellow and red fossil soils, the oldest exposed layers in the park.

image.caption: Yellow Mounds Overlook
image.altText: A small trail proceeds through rolling mounds of striped colors: yellows, reds, whites, browns.

name: Pinnacles Overlook
summary: A wide view south over spires and gullies to the prairie, often with bighorn sheep nearby.

image.caption: Pinnacles Overlook
image.altText: A dramatic Badlands landscape consisting of layered, jagged rock extending into prairie landscape.

name: Roberts Prairie Dog Town
summary: A busy prairie dog colony on the Sage Creek Rim Road.

image.caption: Roberts Prairie Dog Town
image.altText: A wooden sign reads "Roberts Prairie Dog Town" with a small wooden post under a blow sky.

name: Sage Creek Basin Overlook
summary: A view over the wilderness prairie where the park's bison range.

image.caption: Sage Creek Basin Overlook
image.altText: Prairie landscape with mixed grasses and trees extending for miles into horizon under blue sky.

name: Big Badlands Overlook
summary: The first view of the Badlands Wall from the Northeast Entrance, and a sunrise favourite.

image.caption: Big Badlands Overlook
image.altText: A wayside exhibit stands at the edge of drop off into badlands formations

name: Ben Reifel Visitor Center
summary: Located at park headquarters, the Ben Reifel Visitor Center features exhibits, an air conditioned theater,and restroom facilities.

name: White River Visitor Center
summary: The visitor center is located on the Pine Ridge Reservation and offers a staffed information desk, exhibits, restrooms, picnic tables, and water. Impromptu talks are available by request.

name: Sage Creek Campground
summary: Sage Creek Campground is a primitive campground.

name: Cedar Pass Campground
summary: Located near the Ben Reifel Visitor Center, the Cedar Pass Campground has 96 level sites with scenic views of the badlands formations.

name: Santa Elena Canyon
summary: The Rio Grande leaves a 1,500-foot cleft in a wall of limestone; a short trail follows it in.

image.caption: Santa Elena Canyon Trail
image.altText: Santa Elena Canyon Trailhead Exhibit sign and trail

name: The Window
summary: The Chisos Basin's one outlet, a pour-off framing the desert to the west — best at sunset.

image.caption: Window Trail
image.altText: An agave plant grows next to a dirt trail that heads towards a "V" in the surrounding mountains.

name: Lost Mine Trail
summary: A climb through oak and juniper to a ridge with views deep into the Chisos and over Mexico.

image.caption: Lost Mine Trail
image.altText: A mountainside with desert plants and trees with a tall rocky peak in the background

name: Emory Peak
summary: The highest point in the park, reached by a long trail and a short scramble.

image.caption: Emory Peak Trail
image.altText: A trail composed of rock steps climbs the side of a hill covered in yellow flowers.

name: Boquillas Canyon
summary: The river enters a deep limestone canyon at the park's eastern end.

image.caption: Boquillas Canyon
image.altText: A river flows through high walls of limestone, while hikers walk along the sandy banks.

name: Hot Springs
summary: A stone tub of 105°F spring water on the riverbank, beside the ruins of an early tourist resort.

image.caption: Hot Spring Canyon West End
image.altText: A river crosses an open plain before heading into a limestone canyon.

name: Mule Ears
summary: Twin volcanic peaks seen from the Ross Maxwell Scenic Drive.

image.caption: View from Mule Ears Overlook
image.altText: A view across the desert with Mule Ears Peaks in the background.

name: Castolon Historic District
summary: Adobe buildings of a border trading post and army camp, near the river.

image.caption: Castolon Historic District
image.altText: 2-room adobe structure with a metal ramada over the front doors

name: Castolon Visitor Center
summary: Located in the Castolon Historic District, the Castolon Visitor Center is open daily during the winter months. River use permits are issued during normal business hours, and entrance fees can be paid at the Castolon Visitor Center.

name: Chisos Basin Visitor Center
summary: The Chisos Basin Visitor Center includes interactive exhibits on plants, animals, and birds found in the Chisos Mountains. Backcountry and river use permits are issued during normal business hours, and entrance fees can be paid at the visitor center.

name: Panther Junction Visitor Center
summary: Panther Junction Visitor Center is the best place to begin your visit. Backcountry & river use permits are issued here.

name: Persimmon Gap Visitor Center
summary: Persimmon Gap Visitor Center is located in a low pass between the Santiago Mountains at the northern entrance of the park. This pass has been a travel corridor for centuries for people entering and exiting the lower Big Bend country.

name: Rio Grande Village Visitor Center
summary: The Rio Grande Village Visitor Center is located 0.25 miles north of the Rio Grande Village developed area. New exhibits focus on the Rio Grande (how it has changed over time, how the NPS works with our Mexican counterparts to protect and care for it, and the rich assemblage of species that it supports).

name: Chisos Basin Campground
summary: The Chisos Basin Campground is nestled in an open woodland within a scenic mountain basin.

name: Rio Grande Village Campground
summary: Set in a grove of cottonwoods and acacia trees, the Rio Grande Village Campground is located near the Rio Grande.

name: Cottonwood Campground
summary: Cottonwood Campground is a quiet oasis in the western corner of Big Bend National Park.

name: Rio Grande Village RV
summary: Open, paved lot with grassy, tree-lined edges.

name: Boca Chita Key
summary: A small key with an ornamental lighthouse, a harbor and a campground, popular with boaters.

name: Elliott Key
summary: The park's largest island, with a campground, a harbor and a trail through tropical hardwood forest.

name: Maritime Heritage Trail
summary: Shipwrecks on the reef, including the Mandalay in shallow water — a snorkeler's wreck.

image.caption: Mandalay Wreck
image.altText: Man snorkeling a shipwreck lying on the sandy bottom of the ocean

name: Fowey Rocks Lighthouse
summary: A cast-iron lighthouse standing on the reef, seen from boats offshore.

name: Stiltsville
summary: A cluster of houses on pilings in the bay, the last of a once-larger village.

name: Dante Fascell Visitor Center
summary: The Dante Fascell Visitor Center is located at Convoy Point, 9 miles East of the city of Homestead, Florida. A beautiful museum offers a virtual journey through the park's four ecosystems using dioramas, audio and video.

name: Boca Chita Campground
summary: Boca Chita campground is located on an island.

name: Elliott Key Campground
summary: Elliott Key campground is located on an island.

name: Painted Wall
summary: The tallest cliff in Colorado, its dark face streaked with pale pegmatite.

image.caption: View from Painted Wall Overlook
image.altText: View from Painted Wall Overlook

name: Chasm View
summary: The canyon at its narrowest and deepest, straight down from the South Rim.

image.caption: View from Chasm View Overlook
image.altText: View from Chasm View Overlook

name: Gunnison Point
summary: The overlook behind the South Rim Visitor Center, the first big view.

image.caption: Gunnison Point Overlook
image.altText: Gunnison Point Overlook

name: Sunset View
summary: A wide view down canyon at the end of South Rim Drive.

image.caption: Sunset View Overlook
image.altText: Sunset View Overlook

name: Narrows View
summary: On the North Rim, looking down on the canyon's narrowest point.

image.caption: View from Narrows Overlook
image.altText: View from Narrows Overlook

name: Pulpit Rock
summary: A stone platform jutting over the canyon on South Rim Drive.

image.caption: Pulpit Rock Overlook
image.altText: Pulpit Rock Overlook

name: North Rim Ranger Station
summary: The North Rim Ranger Station is open intermittently in summer and closed in winter. In the summer, maps and information are available on the ranger station porch.

name: South Rim Visitor Center
summary: This visitor center has exhibits, information, book and map sales, water (available seasonally), vault toilets, and hiking trailheads. It is open year-round with the exception of Thanksgiving Day, Christmas Day, and New Years Day.

name: South Rim Campground
summary: The South Rim Campground is located one mile (1.6 km) from the South Rim Visitor Center.

name: North Rim Campground
summary: The North Rim Campground is remote and has 13 sites dispersed among pinyon and juniper trees.

name: East Portal Campground
summary: East Portal Campground is located within Curecanti National Recreation Area, but is adjacent to and only accessible from Black Canyon National Park ($30 entrance fee).

name: Sunrise Point
summary: The northern end of Bryce Amphitheater, and the start of the Queen's Garden trail.

image.caption: Sunrise Point
image.altText: A tree with exposed roots stands at the edge of a landscape of red and white rock spires

name: Sunset Point
summary: The amphitheater's centre, looking down on Thor's Hammer and the Navajo Loop.

image.caption: Sunset Point
image.altText: Red and white rock fins stand among distant spires and forested landscape

name: Inspiration Point
summary: Three levels of overlook above the densest crowd of hoodoos.

image.caption: Inspiration Point
image.altText: A vibrant red rock landscape of white limestone and forest below

name: Bryce Point
summary: The amphitheater's southern tip, with the whole of it laid out below.

image.caption: Bryce Point
image.altText: A red rock and forested landscape filled with rock spires

name: Navajo Loop
summary: Switchbacks down into Wall Street, a slot between towering walls, and back up past Thor's Hammer.

name: Queen's Garden
summary: The gentlest way below the rim, among hoodoos named for their likeness to royalty.

image.caption: Queen's Garden Trail
image.altText: A glowing landscape of red and orange rock spires and forest

name: Rainbow Point
summary: The end of the scenic drive and the park's high point, with bristlecone pines on a short loop.

image.caption: Rainbow Point
image.altText: White rock red rock spires and forest at viewpoint

name: Natural Bridge
summary: A span of red rock seen from a pull-out on the scenic drive.

image.caption: Natural Bridge
image.altText: A glowing orange rock arch stands among limestone slopes above a forested landscape

name: Mossy Cave
summary: A short walk outside the main entrance to a waterfall and a damp alcove of moss.

image.caption: Mossy Cave Trail
image.altText: A canyon of red rock lined with trees and shrubs contains a waterfall feeding a small stream

name: Bryce Canyon Visitor Center
summary: The Bryce Canyon Visitor Center might be one of your first stops when visiting Bryce Canyon National Park. Here you can obtain driving and hiking directions beyond those available on this website, weather forecasts, a current schedule of Park Ranger guided programs, Junior Ranger booklets, and information on area services including lodging, dining and other attractions.

name: North Campground
summary: Located across the road from the Visitor Center and is comprised of 100 sites in 4 loops; A, B, C, D.

name: Sunset Campground
summary: Located west of Sunset Point, approximately 1.5 miles south of the Bryce Canyon Visitor Center, and is comprised of 99 sites in 3 loops; Loop A is primarily for RVs; Loops B & C are tent-only.

name: Mesa Arch
summary: A short walk to an arch on the rim's edge that frames the canyons below, famous at sunrise.

name: Grand View Point
summary: The end of the Island in the Sky road, with the White Rim and the canyons spread out below.

image.caption: Grand View Point
image.altText: White snow dusts the tops of the brown and red canyons from Grand View Point

name: Green River Overlook
summary: A view down to the Green River winding through Stillwater Canyon.

image.caption: Sunset at Green River Overlook
image.altText: Two hikers sit on the edge of Green River Overlook at sunset

name: Upheaval Dome
summary: A crater-like ring of upturned rock whose origin is still debated.

image.caption: Upheaval Dome
image.altText: Layers of green, red, beige and orange rock are visible within a crater.

name: Shafer Canyon
summary: The switchbacks of the Shafer Trail road dropping from the mesa to the White Rim.

image.caption: Shafer Trail
image.altText: A light beige, unpaved road winds down a steep, multicolored sandstone canyon.

name: Chesler Park
summary: A grassland ringed by red-and-white spires, reached on foot in the Needles.

image.caption: Chesler Park Viewpoint
image.altText: A hiker sits atop a sandstone rock looking out across a vast view of sandstone spires.

name: Druid Arch
summary: A tall, slotted arch at the head of Elephant Canyon, a long day hike in the Needles.

image.caption: Druid Arch
image.altText: A large sandstone arch looms across the skyline on a bright, sunny blue sky day.

name: Horseshoe Canyon
summary: A detached unit of the park, home to the Great Gallery of Barrier Canyon-style rock art.

name: Canyonlands Backcountry Office
summary: The central backcountry office is located at park administrative offices south of Moab. Rangers can answer questions about backcountry travel over phone or email and issue permits online.
hours: Rangers are normally available five days a week to answer questions over the phone or email and issue permits online.

name: Hans Flat Ranger Station
summary: The remote Hans Flat (Maze) Ranger Station is normally open daily year-round. This ranger contact station has a picnic table and vault toilet, and a small selection of books and maps for sale.

name: Island in the Sky Visitor Center
summary: The Island in the Sky Visitor Center offers exhibits, book & map sales, park orientation film, backcountry permits, general information, vault toilets, and park rangers on duty. You can get drinking water inside (during open hours) or outside (24 hours a day) during summer and fall.

name: The Needles Visitor Center
summary: The Needles Visitor Center normally offers exhibits, book & map sales, backcountry permits, information, picnic area, and park rangers on duty. The park orientation movie (15 minutes) is available on demand.

name: The Needles Campground
summary: The Needles Campground has 26 individual sites.

name: Island in the Sky (Willow Flat) Campground
summary: Island in the Sky Campground (Willow Flat) has 12 sites, first-come, first-served.

name: The Needles District Group Campsites
summary: The Needles district has three group campsites in different locations, which can accommodate up to 15, 25, or 50 campers (respectively).

name: Fruita orchards
summary: Historic orchards along the Fremont River, open for picking when the fruit is ripe.

image.caption: Apricots in the Gifford Orchard
image.altText: apricots on a tree. An old barn and red cliffs in the background

name: Gifford House
summary: A Fruita farmhouse where pies and preserves are sold in season.

image.caption: Gifford House
image.altText: a small farmhouse with two sets of steps each leading up to a door

name: Petroglyph Panel
summary: Fremont carvings of figures and bighorn sheep, seen from boardwalks beside the highway.

name: Capitol Dome
summary: The white sandstone dome that gave the park its name.

image.caption: Capitol Dome and the Fremont River
image.altText: Large rounded white sandstone dome centered above a river, with green grass, red cliffs, & blue sky

name: Scenic Drive
summary: A paved road south along the face of the fold, with spurs into Grand Wash and Capitol Gorge.

image.caption: Scenic Drive
image.altText: a road parallels sandstone cliffs

name: Hickman Bridge
summary: A natural bridge of sandstone, reached by a two-mile round-trip trail from the highway.

name: Cathedral Valley
summary: Freestanding monoliths in the park's remote north, reached by dirt road; the Temples of the Sun and Moon stand here.

image.caption: The Cathedrals
image.altText: large reddish brown monoliths rise from the desert floor

name: Panorama Point
summary: A wide view across the fold to the Henry Mountains, and a dark-sky site at night.

image.caption: Panorama point stormy sunset
image.altText: Juniper trees dot the foreground, with distant red-brown cliffs and colorful cloudy sky at sunset.

name: Capitol Reef National Park Visitor Center
summary: Capitol Reef National Park visitor center sits at the intersection of UT-24 and the Scenic Drive.

name: Primitive campsites at Cathedral Campground
summary: It is located approximately halfway on the Cathedral Valley Loop Road.

name: Primitive campsites at Cedar Mesa Campground
summary: It is located approximately 23 miles (37.0 km) south of Utah State Highway 24 on the Notom-Bullfrog Road and is at 5,500 feet (1,676 m) in elevation.

name: Group Campsite
summary: The Group Campsite is a secluded site located near the Fruita Campground and can accommodate a maximum of 40 people.

name: Fruita Campground
summary: The 71 site Fruita campground is the only developed campground in the park, offering picnic tables, fire rings, restrooms, water and a dump station.

name: Natural Entrance
summary: A steep, paved trail that descends about 750 feet into the cavern, past the Devil's Spring and Iceberg Rock.

image.caption: Natural Entrance
image.altText: Photo of the Natural Entrance to Carlsbad Cavern with a trail zigzagging down.

name: The Big Room
summary: The largest cave chamber in North America, on a mile-long loop trail among giant formations.

image.caption: Big Room
image.altText: A photo of the Big Room with thousands of formations.

name: Bat Flight
summary: At dusk from late spring to autumn, the bats' evening flight from the amphitheater at the natural entrance.

image.caption: Natural Entrance
image.altText: Photo of the Natural Entrance to Carlsbad Cavern with a trail zigzagging down.

name: Rattlesnake Springs
summary: A spring-fed oasis of cottonwoods, one of the best birding spots in New Mexico.

image.caption: Rattlesnake Springs
image.altText: Photo of the grassy area and large cottonwood trees at Rattlesnake Springs.

name: Visitor Center
summary: >> RESERVATIONS REQUIRED to enter cavern and must be purchased at recreation.gov or by calling 877-444-6777. The reservation is only for selecting the entry time.

name: Inspiration Point
summary: The view west along Anacapa's chain of islets, with Santa Cruz beyond.

name: Scorpion Ranch
summary: The landing on Santa Cruz, with an old ranch, a campground and trails up onto the cliffs.

name: Potato Harbor
summary: A cove below sheer cliffs, reached on a walk from Scorpion Anchorage.

name: Cavern Point
summary: A loop over Santa Cruz's sea cliffs, good for spotting whales in season.

name: Painted Cave
summary: One of the largest sea caves in the world, on Santa Cruz's north shore, seen by kayak or boat.

name: Torrey Pines
summary: A grove of one of the rarest pines in the country, on Santa Rosa's east coast.

name: Point Bennett
summary: San Miguel's western tip, where tens of thousands of seals and sea lions haul out.

name: Channel Islands National Park Visitor Center
summary: The Robert J. Lagomarsino Visitor Center at Channel Islands National Park features a bookstore, a display of marine aquatic life, and exhibits featuring the unique character of each park island.

name: Outdoors Santa Barbara Visitor Center
summary: The small Outdoors Santa Barbara Visitor Center not only has one of the best views of Santa Barbara, but also offers visitors information about Channel Islands National Park, Channel Islands National Marine Sanctuary, Santa Barbara Maritime Museum, and the City of Santa Barbara. Open 10:30 am until 4:30 pm daily.

name: San Miguel Island Ranger and Visitor Contact Station
summary: The visitor contact and ranger station is only open when staff is present.

name: Santa Barbara Island Visitor Center
summary: A small visitor center is located on the island. Features include displays on the natural and cultural resources of the island.

name: Santa Rosa Island Visitor Contact Station
summary: The historic schoolhouse is now home to this small visitor contact station with exhibits on the ranching history of Santa Rosa Island.

name: Scorpion Ranch Visitor Center on Santa Cruz Island
summary: The small visitor center resides in the historic Scorpion Ranch house which was constructed in 1886-1887.

name: Visitor Center Anacapa Island
summary: Once the historic Coast Guard general services building (workshop and garage), this Mission Revival style building now serves as a small visitor center that features include displays on the natural and cultural resources of the island and the original lead-crystal Fresnel lens from the Anacapa Lighthouse.

name: Anacapa Island Campground
summary: Primitive camping is available (seven sites; $15 per night per site; reservations required).

name: Scorpion Canyon Campground
summary: Primitive camping is available (25 individual sites at $15 per night-per site and 6 group sites at $40 per night-per site; reservations required).

name: Del Norte Backcountry Campground
summary: The Santa Cruz Island Del Norte Backcountry Campground is currently the only backcountry campground on Santa Cruz Island.

name: Water Canyon Campground
summary: Primitive camping is available (15 sites; $15 per night per site; reservations required).

name: Santa Rosa Island Backcountry Beach Camping
summary: Backcountry camping on Santa Rosa Island is currently limited to certain beaches between August 15th and December 31st.

name: San Miguel Island Campground
summary: Primitive camping is available (nine sites; $15 per night per site; reservations required).

name: Santa Barbara Island Campground
summary: Primitive camping is available (seven sites; $15 per night per site; reservations required).

name: Boardwalk Loop
summary: A 2.6-mile raised boardwalk through old-growth bottomland forest and past cypress knees, from the visitor center.

name: Weston Lake
summary: An oxbow lake on the Weston Lake Loop, with cypress growing in the water.

name: Cedar Creek
summary: A blackwater creek through the forest, followed by a marked canoe and kayak trail.

name: Harry Hampton Visitor Center
summary: Open 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. daily. Closed New Year's Day, Washington's Birthday, Columbus Day, Thanksgiving Day, and Christmas Day.

name: Longleaf Campground
summary: The Longleaf Campground offers walk up campsites for visitors wishing to camp in the frontcountry of Congaree.

name: Bluff Campground
summary: The Bluff Campground is a hike in campground and is perfect for those looking to camp in the frontcountry yet have a more backcountry experience.

name: Rim Village
summary: The lodge, the visitor center and the Sinnott Memorial Overlook, built into the caldera wall.

image.caption: View of Sinnott Memorial from the rim
image.altText: View of Sinnott Memorial from the rim

name: Wizard Island
summary: A cinder cone rising from the lake, reached by tour boat in summer.

name: Phantom Ship
summary: A small island of ancient lava shaped like a ship under sail.

image.caption: Phantom Ship at Sunset
image.altText: View of the Phantom Ship at sunset, one of two islands in Crater Lake.

name: Cleetwood Cove
summary: The only trail to the shore: a steep mile down to the water, where swimming is allowed.

name: Watchman Peak
summary: A short climb to a fire lookout above Wizard Island, the best sunset view in the park.

name: Mount Scott
summary: The park's highest point, a trail to a fire lookout with the whole lake below.

name: Pinnacles
summary: Spires of welded volcanic ash in a canyon in the park's southeast corner.

image.caption: Pinnacles
image.altText: Spires of hardened volcanic matter are exposed via erosion along a canyon wall

name: Pumice Desert

name: Thurmond Depot Visitor Center

name: War Ridge/Backus Mountain Campground
summary: This is the only campground in the park that is not along the river.

name: Stone Cliff
summary: This tent only campground located near the historic railroad town of Thurmond offers 7 walk-in sites, 5 on the sandy beach of the New River and 2 in the nearby forest.

name: Thayer Campground
summary: This tent only campground is located near the community of Thayer along the banks of the New River.

name: Glade Creek Campground
summary: This forested campground offers both tent and RV sites near the banks of the New River and the Glade Creek Trailhead.

name: Grandview Sandbar
summary: This campground offers shaded wooded campsites near the banks of the New River.

name: Army Camp
summary: This campground offers both tent and RV campsites along the banks of the New River at one of its many horseshoe bends.

name: Brooklyn Campground
summary: This tent only campground is located on the banks of the New River near the Cunard River Access point and Southside Trailhead.

name: Burnwood Group Campsite
summary: Burnwood is located across Route 19 from Canyon Rim Visitor Center and offers group camping.

name: Meadow Creek Campground
summary: This primitive campground located along the New River is only one mile from the Sandstone Visitor Center.

name: Diablo Lake Overlook
summary: The best-known view in the park: a turquoise lake between forested peaks, beside the highway.

image.caption: Diablo Lake Overlook
image.altText: A blue lake surrounded by forested mountains.

name: Cascade Pass
summary: A climb to a high pass among glaciers and meadows, used by travellers for millennia.

image.caption: Cascade Pass Trail
image.altText: Three hikers travel a dirt path on the side of a steep grassy slope, with mountains in the distance.

name: Ross Lake
summary: A long reservoir reached by trail from the highway, with a floating resort.

name: Gorge Creek Falls
summary: A waterfall pouring into the Skagit gorge, seen from a short walk at the highway.

image.caption: Gorge Creek Falls
image.altText: A waterfall flows through a steep, rocky gorge.

name: Thunder Knob
summary: A short climb to views over Diablo Lake and the surrounding peaks.

image.caption: Thunder Knob View
image.altText: A blue lake surrounded by forested mountains.

name: Sourdough Mountain
summary: A steep trail to a fire lookout high above Diablo.

image.caption: Sourdough Mountain
image.altText: A hiker stands looking at a scenic mountain view.

name: Stehekin
summary: A remote valley community at the head of Lake Chelan, reached by boat, plane or trail.

image.caption: North Cascades Lodge at Stehekin
image.altText: A wooden deck with tables and chairs outside a building.

name: Rainbow Falls
summary: A tall waterfall a short ride up the valley from Stehekin.

image.caption: Rainbow Falls
image.altText: A thin waterfall drops down a gray cliff face.

name: Buckner Orchard
summary: A homestead orchard in the Stehekin valley, still producing apples.

image.caption: Buckner Orchard
image.altText: A rusted pickup truck from the 1940s sits in a field and open forest

name: Forest Info Center with HQ Administration Building
summary: The North Cascades National Park Service Complex Headquarters (Administrative Offices) is five miles east of I-5 in Burlington and 46 miles west of the North Cascades National Park Service Complex boundary.

name: Golden West Visitor Center
summary: Visitor Center located short walk from the passenger ferry landing at Stehekin Landing inside what was the historic Golden West Lodge.

name: North Cascades Visitor Center
summary: Location: Across the Skagit River from the North Cascades Highway (State Route 20) near milepost 120 and the town of Newhalem. Adjacent to Newhalem Creek Campground.

name: Wilderness Information Center
summary: The Wilderness Information Center is the main backcountry permit office for North Cascades National Park and the adjacent Ross Lake and Lake Chelan National Recreation Areas. Backcountry permits are required for overnights in the park year-round and are available at an outdoor self-issue station when the center is closed during the winter season.

name: Newhalem Creek Campground
summary: Newhalem Creek Campground is a comfortable facility close to the town of Newhalem and the Skagit River.

name: Goodell Creek Campground
summary: Goodell Creek Campground is situated in lush, old growth forest on the banks of the Skagit River.

name: Lower Goodell Group Campground
summary: Lower Goodell Group Campground is a convenient campground on the banks of Goodell Creek.

name: Gorge Lake Campground
summary: Gorge Lake Campground is located on the bank of Gorge Lake, next to the cascading Stetattle Creek and is a primitive camp with no water.

name: Colonial Creek North Campground
summary: Colonial Creek North Campground is a remote, yet bustling campground nestled in old growth forest.

name: Colonial Creek South Campground
summary: Colonial Creek South Campground is a remote, yet busy campground nestled in old growth forest on the south side of State Route 20 near mile marker 130.Ten walk-in, tent-only sites are available first-come, first-served in the winter (sites 64-73).

name: Lakeview Campground
summary: Located at the head of Lake Chelan, Lakeview Campground is a five-minute walk from the boat dock at Stehekin Landing.

name: Purple Point Campground
summary: Located at the head of Lake Chelan, Purple Point Campground is a ten-minute walk from the boat dock at Stehekin Landing.

name: Harlequin Campground
summary: Harlequin Campground is located near Stehekin in Lake Chelan National Recreation Area, 4.5 miles up the Stehekin Valley Rd from Stehekin Landing and 0.5 miles from the public airstrip.

name: Hozomeen Campground
summary: Hozomeen Campground is located at the north end of Ross Lake and is open from late May through October.

name: Hurricane Ridge
summary: A ridge-top road and trails with views across the Olympic Mountains to Mount Olympus.

name: Hall of Mosses
summary: A short loop through moss-draped maples and spruce in the Hoh Rain Forest.

image.caption: Mossy branch
image.altText: A tree branch heavy with moss

name: Quinault Big Sitka Spruce
summary: One of the largest Sitka spruces known, near Lake Quinault.

name: Lake Crescent
summary: A deep, clear glacial lake with a historic lodge.

name: Marymere Falls
summary: A slender waterfall through old forest, a short walk from Lake Crescent.

name: Sol Duc Falls
summary: A waterfall that splits into several channels in a mossy gorge.

name: Rialto Beach
summary: A driftwood-strewn beach of sea stacks, with Hole-in-the-Wall arch at low tide.

name: Ruby Beach
summary: A coastal beach of sea stacks and driftwood on the Kalaloch coast.

name: Second Beach
summary: A forest trail to a beach of sea stacks and tide pools near La Push.

name: Hoh Rain Forest Visitor Center
summary: Located in the Hoh Rain Forest. The visitor center is open daily during the summer and intermittently during the winter.
hours: Visitor information, exhibits, passport stamping station, book store.

name: Hurricane Ridge Visitor Contact Station
summary: While the historic Hurricane Ridge Day Lodge was destroyed in a fire, the small but mighty Visitor Contact Station is here to help! While rangers are present to answer questions during open hours in summer, please be aware there is no indoor space for visitors or running water available.

name: Kalaloch Ranger Station
summary: See you in 2027! Kalaloch Ranger Station is open daily during the summer and closed the rest of the year.

name: Olympic National Park Visitor Center
summary: This is the main Visitor Center and Wilderness Information Center for Olympic National Park. Park staff are available daily at the visitor center, and by phone (360-565-3130) or email.

name: Quinault Rain Forest Ranger Station
summary: See you in 2027! Quinault Rain Forest Ranger Station is open Thursdays-Mondays during the summer and closed during the rest of the year.

name: Kalaloch Campround
summary: Oceanside camp at Kalaloch with some sites overlooking the Pacific Ocean.

name: Queets Campground
summary: Relax in this secluded campground near the Queets River.

name: Ozette Campground
summary: Adjacent to Lake Ozette, this small campground is great for those that enjoy lakeside camping and water activities

name: Mora Campground
summary: Situated in a coastal forest, some sites offer views views of the Quillayute River.

name: North Fork Campground
summary: Surrounded by temperate rain forest, this small and remote campground is a great spot for campers seeking solitude.

name: South Beach Campground
summary: Positioned on a bluff overlooking the Pacific Ocean, South Beach offers panoramic ocean views and beach access.

name: Staircase Campground
summary: Camp near the Skokomish River and enjoy old-growth forest at Staircase.

name: Graves Creek Campground
summary: Located in the Quinault Rain Forest, relax near a serene stream at Graves Creek Campground.

name: Hoh Campground
summary: Surround yourself with moss and ancient trees in this temperate rain forest.

name: Heart O' the Hills Campground
summary: Surrounded by old growth forest, Heart O' the Hills offers summer ranger programs and great family fun

name: Fairholme Campground
summary: Neighboring Lake Crescent, Fairholme includes lakeside campsites and a nearby boat launch.

name: Deer Park Campground
summary: At 5,400 feet in elevation, Deer Park boasts mountain views and starry skies.

name: Blue Mesa
summary: A loop down among blue, grey and purple badlands strewn with petrified wood.

image.caption: Visitors on the Blue Mesa Trail
image.altText: Hikers walk amidst gray, blue, and purple badlands along a trail under a blue sky.

name: Crystal Forest
summary: A paved loop through logs with sparkling quartz and amethyst crystals.

image.caption: Crystal Forest Trail
image.altText: Multiple tan petrified logs gather along the Crystal Forest Trail under a blue sky.

name: Giant Logs
summary: Some of the park's largest logs, behind the Rainbow Forest Museum.

image.caption: Visitors on Giant Logs Trail
image.altText: Hikers walking on trail through grassland and pieces of petrified wood, mostly cloudy sky above.

name: Agate Bridge
summary: A petrified log spanning a small ravine, braced by concrete in the early 1900s.

image.caption: Agate Bridge
image.altText: A large petrified log spans a pale sandstone gully with grasslands in the distance.

name: Agate House
summary: A small Ancestral Puebloan dwelling built from blocks of petrified wood.

image.caption: Agate House
image.altText: Reconstructed Ancestral Puebloan village of petrified wood pieces.

name: Puerco Pueblo
summary: Remains of a pueblo of about a hundred rooms, with petroglyphs nearby.

image.caption: Puerco Pueblo
image.altText: Puerco Pueblo masonry walls just after sunset with a partly cloudy sky, mesa in the background.

name: Painted Desert Inn
summary: A historic Route 66 inn with murals by the Hopi artist Fred Kabotie, now a museum.

image.caption: Painted Desert Inn NHL
image.altText: Historic Pueblo-Revival style building sitting on the edge of a mesa above the Painted Desert

name: Tawa Point
summary: A rim overlook across the colourful Painted Desert badlands.

image.caption: Tawa Point
image.altText: Overlooking white and red badlands from mesa edge at twilight, blue sky.

name: Painted Desert Inn
summary: In its almost 100 years overlooking the Painted Desert, the inn has undergone many changes. The original building from the early 1920s was made of petrified wood.

name: Painted Desert Visitor Center
summary: Painted Desert Visitor Center is located at exit #311 off of I-40 is closed for construction. Follow signs to the Painted Desert Inn.

name: Rainbow Forest Museum
summary: Rainbow Forest Museum provides exhibits of petrified wood, fossils, and displays of prehistoric animals as well as information, book sales, and restrooms.

name: High Peaks
summary: A strenuous loop over the spires, with a section of carved steps and handrails along narrow ledges. The best place to watch for condors.

image.caption: Steep and Narrow Section of High Peaks
image.altText: Metal handrails follow a narrow trail through misty volcanic rock formations and boulders.

name: Bear Gulch Cave
summary: A talus cave on the east side, partly or wholly closed at times to protect its bat colony. Bring a torch.

image.caption: Bear Gulch Cave
image.altText: View of a large boulder and rock carved steps adjacent a handrail underneath a rock roofed canyon.

name: Balconies Cave
summary: A talus cave on the west side under the Balconies cliffs. Bring a torch; it can flood in winter.

image.caption: Balconies Cave
image.altText: Narrow rock passage in Balconies Cave with daylight visible through an opening above.

name: Bear Gulch Reservoir
summary: A small lake held back by a 1930s dam, above the Bear Gulch Cave.

image.caption: Bear Gulch Reservoir
image.altText: Steep rocks next to a stone dam and reservoir reflecting the rocks

name: Moses Spring
summary: A short trail through a shaded canyon to the Bear Gulch Cave and reservoir.

image.caption: Moses Spring
image.altText: Spring trickling out of the bottom of rock wall.

name: Bear Gulch Nature Center
summary: Hey ranger, what plant is this? Hey ranger, what do condors look like?

name: Pinnacles Park Store
summary: Get your passport stamped and buy the official park souvenirs, all at the park store! Located in the Pinnacles campground, the store is open everyday, from 9:00 AM to 4:00 PM, including holidays.

name: West Pinnacles Visitor Contact Station
summary: Get your park souvenirs and plan your visit all in one place! Please note that this visitor center may be closed seasonally due to available staffing.
hours: The West Pinnacles contact station is open daily depending on available staffing.

name: Pinnacles Campground
summary: Pinnacles Campground is run by Pinnacles Recreation Company.

name: Tall Trees Grove
summary: A grove of very tall redwoods beside Redwood Creek. Reached by a steep trail from a gated road that needs a free permit.

image.caption: Tall Trees Trail Tour Stop 1
image.altText: Tall Trees Trail Tour Stop 1 marker.

name: Lady Bird Johnson Grove
summary: A short loop through old growth on a ridge above the coast, named for the former first lady.

image.caption: Hiker's Bridge At Trailhead
image.altText: A brown wooden bridge crosses a road. Trees crowd the scene

name: Fern Canyon
summary: A creek ravine about 50 feet deep with walls covered in ferns, near Gold Bluffs Beach. Expect wet feet.

name: Stout Memorial Grove
summary: A level loop among some of the largest redwoods, beside the Smith River.

name: Simpson-Reed Grove
summary: An easy loop through old-growth redwood and hemlock just off US 199.

name: Big Tree Wayside
summary: A short walk to one of the park's largest redwoods, off the Newton B. Drury Scenic Parkway.

image.caption: Big Tree Wayside
image.altText: People stand next to redwood tree and a viewing deck. Orientation signs in the foreground.

name: Klamath River Overlook
summary: A high viewpoint over the river mouth; watch for grey whales on their migrations.

image.caption: Klamath River Mouth
image.altText: Blue-green ocean and a sandspit at the mouth of a river.

name: Gold Bluffs Beach
summary: A long, wild beach backed by bluffs, often with elk in the grass.

image.caption: Gold Bluffs Beach Day Use Area
image.altText: A brown, wooden information sign and safety signs are on grassy dunes.

name: Elk Meadow
summary: A meadow near Orick where Roosevelt elk often graze, and the start of the Trillium Falls Trail.

image.caption: Elk Meadow Day Use Area viewing platform
image.altText: Two interpretive panels and views of meadow and a paved trail.

name: Crescent City Information Center
summary: Located in the bottom floor of park headquarters. Picnic area and retail sales.

name: Hiouchi Visitor Center
summary: Northern-most park visitor center located 9-miles east of Crescent City on Hwy 199. Exhibits about Tolowa culture and art, redwood ecology, park information, junior ranger program, bookstore and retail sales.

name: Jedediah Smith Visitor Center
summary: Located in the Jedediah Smith Redwoods State Park campground, near the amphitheater. Small visitor center with information, exhibits, junior ranger program, bookstore, and retail sales.

name: Prairie Creek Visitor Center
summary: Located just off the Newton B. Drury Scenic Parkway - in the heart of Prairie Creek Redwoods State Park.

name: Thomas H. Kuchel Visitor Center
summary: Southern-most visitor center in the park and located right on the beach. Exhibits about Yurok culture, art and history, redwood ecology, park information, junior ranger program, bookstore and retail sales.

name: Jedediah Smith Campground - Jedediah Smith Redwoods State Park
summary: Situated in a magnificent old-growth redwood grove on the banks of the wild and scenic Smith River, this campground offers hiking trails, swimming, fishing, and seasonal campfire programs.

name: Mill Creek Campground - Del Norte Coast Redwoods State Park
summary: Sleep beneath towering maples and young redwoods.

name: Gold Bluffs Beach Campground - Prairie Creek Redwoods State Park
summary: Experience the wild Pacific coastline and grazing Roosevelt elk in this campground, with easy access to a secluded stretch of beach, Fern Canyon, and 70 miles of hiking and biking trails.

name: Elk Prairie Campground - Prairie Creek Redwoods State Park
summary: Enjoy ancient coast redwoods, grazing Roosevelt elk and black-tailed deer in Elk Prairie, easy access to over 70 miles of hiking and biking trails, and seasonal ranger-led programs.

name: Bear Lake
summary: A subalpine lake at the end of Bear Lake Road, with an easy loop and trails on to Nymph, Dream and Emerald Lakes.

image.caption: Bear Lake in winter
image.altText: Bear Lake, the surface of the lake is frozen and covered with snow on a sunny day

name: Sprague Lake

image.caption: Sprague Lake Trail in winter
image.altText: A section of the Sprague Lake Trail and lake is covered with snow

summary: A family homestead and guest ranch from the early 1900s in the Kawuneeche Valley.

image.caption: Welcome to the Holzwarth Historic Site
image.altText: A group of park visitors are standing in front of a historic cabin in the Holzwarth Historic Site

name: Longs Peak
summary: The park's highest summit. Its Keyhole Route is a long, exposed scramble, not a hike; climbers set out before dawn.

name: Alpine Visitor Center
summary: Alpine Visitor Center is closed for the season. Located at the top of Fall River Pass and accessed via Trail Ridge Road, Alpine Visitor Center is the highest elevation visitor center in the National Park System at 11,796 feet above sea level.

name: Beaver Meadows Visitor Center
summary: Beaver Meadows Visitor Center is open year-round. This visitor center is located on the east side of RMNP near the town of Estes Park, along U.S.

name: Fall River Visitor Center
summary: The Fall River Visitor Center is located west of the town of Estes Park on U.S. Highway 34, just before the Fall River Entrance to RMNP.

name: Holzwarth Historic Site
summary: Explore the Holzwarth Historic Site, where the Never Summer Ranch and the Holzwarth Trout Lodge was operated by the Holzwarth family through multiple generations from the 1910s to 1970s. Located on the west side of Rocky Mountain National Park eight miles east of (12.8 km) the Kawuneeche Visitor Center.
hours: Welcome to the Holzwarth Historic Site.

name: Information Office
summary: Have questions about Rocky Mountain National Park? Call the Information Office!

name: Junior Ranger Headquarters at Hidden Valley
summary: Junior Ranger Headquarters has closed for the season. We invite you to get out and explore the Hidden Valley area on your own with your family.

name: Kawuneeche Visitor Center
summary: Open daily, the Kawuneeche Visitor Center is located along U.S. Highway 34 on the west side of RMNP, north of the town of Grand Lake.

name: Moraine Park Discovery Center
summary: The Nature Store in the Moraine Park Discovery Center is open daily. This store is managed by Rocky Mountain Conservancy.

name: Sheep Lakes Information Station
summary: Sheep Lakes, located in Horseshoe Park, is a great place to view wildlife. This parking area and viewpoint are open year-round daily 24 hours a day.

name: Wilderness Office
summary: Have questions about planning for an overnight backpacking camping trip? Ready to pick up your backpacking permits?

name: Aspenglen Campground
summary: Aspenglen Campground is open for the summer!

name: Glacier Basin Campground
summary: If planning to camp in RMNP, please see Aspenglen, Timber Creek or Moraine Park Campgrounds.

name: Timber Creek Campground
summary: Timber Creek Campground is open for the summer!

name: Moraine Park Campground
summary: Moraine Park Campground is open for summer camping.

name: Longs Peak Campground
summary: If planning to camp inside RMNP, please check availability at Aspenglen, Timber Creek, or Moraine Park Campgrounds.

image.caption: Pull-off along Cactus Forest Loop Drive

summary: An easy walk through the cactus forest with views to Mica Mountain.

image.caption: Mica View Trailhead, from Picnic Area
image.altText: A small metal sign in the lower right reads "Mica View Trail" A dirt trail stretches off to the left
