Mount Rishiri (利尻山)
summary: A 1,721-metre volcanic cone climbed from Oshidomari on the north coast or Kutsugata on the west. A long, eroded climb for experienced hikers.

name: Himenuma (姫沼)
summary: A small pond in the woods on Rishiri's north side, circled by a short path with the mountain reflected in it on still days.

name: Otatomari-numa (オタトマリ沼)
summary: Rishiri's largest pond, about a kilometre round, on the south-east coast, with a path round it and the mountain reflected in it.

name: Momodai-Nekodai viewpoint (桃台猫台展望台)
summary: On southern Rebun, looking at the 250-metre Momoiwa and the Nekoiwa stack, near the flower-lined Momoiwa trail.

name: Cape Sukoton (スコトン岬)
summary: Rebun's northern tip, looking out to Todo-jima where sea lions haul out. The start of the clifftop trail by Cape Gorota and Cape Sukai.

name: Rebun atsumorisō colony (レブンアツモリソウ群生地)
summary: A slope in northern Rebun where boardwalks pass close to the island's rare cream-coloured lady's-slipper orchid.

name: Panke-numa (パンケ沼)
summary: The largest lake on the Sarobetsu Plain, eight kilometres round and stained red by iron from the peat, with Rishiri on the horizon.

name: Hamayūchi (浜勇知園地)
summary: A dune-coast stop on the road south of Wakkanai, with daylilies and water lilies in early summer and Rishiri across the sea.

name: Sarobetsu Wetland Center
summary: On the raised bog in Toyotomi, with a boardwalk loop of about a kilometre through daylilies, cranberry and sundews.

name: Horonobe Visitor Center
summary: Exhibits and films on how the Sarobetsu bog formed, with an upstairs deck looking towards Rishiri. Closed November to April.

name: Shiretoko Goko (知床五湖)
summary: Five small lakes in old-growth forest below the Shiretoko range, reached by an 800-metre elevated boardwalk or, with a lecture or guide, a ground path.

name: Furepe Falls (フレペの滝)
summary: Groundwater seeping from a cliff about a hundred metres high straight into the sea, on a two-kilometre loop walk from the Nature Center.

name: Kamuiwakka Yu-no-taki (カムイワッカ湯の滝)
summary: A stream warmed by hot springs from Iōzan, tumbling over a series of falls. Climbing it must be booked ahead; the road is closed to private cars in high summer.

name: Mount Rausu (羅臼岳)
summary: The peninsula's highest peak, 1,660 metres. More than eight hours there and back, with snow on the route until late July.

name: Shiretoko Pass (知床峠)
summary: The 738-metre high point of the road between Utoro and Rausu, facing Mount Rausu with Kunashiri across the strait.

name: Lake Rausu (羅臼湖)
summary: The peninsula's largest lake, reached by a path past four smaller ponds. The Ministry advises the same gear as for a mountain hike.

name: Kumagoe Falls (熊越の滝)
summary: A waterfall above Rausu reached by a short stream-side path, with native water crowfoot flowering in the current.

name: Cape Shiretoko (知床岬)
summary: The peninsula's tip: grassland above the Sea of Okhotsk with no road or path. Seen from sightseeing boats out of Utoro.

name: Shiretoko World Heritage Conservation Center
summary: The Ministry's centre at the Utoro roadside station: exhibits, current bear and road information, and the Utoro ranger office.

name: Shiretoko Nature Center
summary: On the road to Shiretoko Goko: the start of the Furepe Falls walk, gear hire, and the shuttle stop for Kamuiwakka.

name: Shiretoko Goko Field House
summary: Where the ground-path lectures are held and registered-guide tours start. Open from late April into November.

name: Shiretoko Rausu Visitor Center
summary: The east-side centre near Rausu Onsen, with an orca skeleton, bear-spray hire and the times of the nearby geyser.

name: Shiretoko World Heritage Rusa Field House
summary: On the coast road north of Rausu, the base for the roadless north-east shore beyond. Open May to October.

name: Lake Akan (阿寒湖)
summary: The caldera lake of the marimo, with Oakandake across the water. Sightseeing boats run to a marimo exhibition on Churui Island.

name: Meakandake (雌阿寒岳)
summary: An active volcano south-west of Lake Akan with fuming craters at the top. Three trails, one starting from Lake Onneto. Check the alert level first.

name: Onneto (オンネトー)
summary: A small lake at the park's western edge whose colour shifts from emerald to deep blue with the light, wind and season.

name: Lake Mashu First Observatory (摩周第一展望台)
summary: The most visited of three viewpoints on the rim above Lake Mashu, beside the Mashu-ko Kamui Terrace rest house. Often in fog or above a sea of cloud.

name: Kaminoko-ike (神の子池)
summary: A small pond of clear, vivid blue water in the forest north of the Mashu caldera, added to the park in 2017.

name: Atosanupuri (アトサヌプリ)
summary: Mount Iō: a bare, active volcano with more than 1,500 steam vents crusted in yellow sulphur, once mined. Reached from Kawayu Onsen on foot.

name: Wakoto Peninsula (和琴半島)
summary: A small volcano jutting into Lake Kussharo, ringed by a 2.5-kilometre trail past steaming vents at Oyakotsu Jigoku.

name: Bihoro Pass (美幌峠)
summary: A roadside station and lookout on the Kussharo caldera rim, over the whole lake to Atosanupuri and, on clear days, the Shiretoko range.

name: Akanko-han Visitor Center
summary: The Ministry's centre for the Akan side, at Akanko Onsen, with live marimo and lake fish. Start of the lakeside walk to the bokke mud pots.

name: Akanko Marimukan
summary: Tourist information in the middle of Akanko Onsen, open daily, with snowshoe and cross-country ski hire in winter.

name: Kawayu Visitor Center
summary: The centre for the Mashu and Kussharo side, at Kawayu Onsen, and the start of the Tsutsujigahara trail to Atosanupuri.

name: Wakoto Field House
summary: Displays on the wildlife of the Wakoto Peninsula, at the neck of the peninsula. Closed from November to mid-April.

name: Hosooka Observatory (細岡展望台)
summary: Known as the 'great view': the whole marsh and the Kushiro River's loops from the eastern hills, with the Akan mountains beyond. Good at sunset.

name: Onnenai boardwalk (温根内木道)
summary: The only path out onto the marsh: a boardwalk from the Onnenai Visitor Center, with bog plants, flowers and birds close at hand.

name: Lake Toro (塘路湖)
summary: An eastern lake with a lakeside path, guided canoe tours down the dam-free Kushiro River, and ice fishing for smelt in winter.

name: Sarubo and Sarurun observatories (サルボ展望台・サルルン展望台)
summary: A wooded hill walk to two lookouts over the lakes and marsh of the eastern side — a different view from the other observatories.

name: Kottaro Shitsugen Observatory (コッタロ湿原展望台)
summary: Steps up from the road across the north of the marsh to a view over spring-fed wetland. Cranes are sometimes seen with binoculars.

name: Yumegaoka Observatory (夢ヶ丘展望台)
summary: At the top of a steep 2.3-kilometre trail north of Lake Takkobu, past sedge tussocks and springs, looking over the river and the railway.

name: Hokuto Site (北斗遺跡)
summary: Pit-dwelling remains from the Palaeolithic to the Satsumon period on the marsh's western edge, with five houses rebuilt.

name: Onnenai Visitor Center
summary: Start of the Onnenai boardwalk, with current nature notes and a cut-through of a sedge tussock.

name: Lake Toro Eco-museum Center 'Arukotto'
summary: Start of the Lake Toro shore path, with displays on water as the lifeline of the wetland.

name: Shirarutoro Nature Center
summary: Displays on the restoration project and the wildlife of Lake Shirarutoro. Closed in winter.

name: Kushiro Shitsugen Wildlife Center
summary: The Ministry's centre for rare birds, with exhibits on fish owls and sea eagles and birds that can no longer return to the wild.

name: Asahidake (旭岳)
summary: Hokkaido's highest peak, 2,291 metres. The ropeway from Asahidake Onsen reaches Sugatami, with a loop past steaming vents and ponds and a 2½-hour path to the top.

name: Sugatami Pond (姿見の池)
summary: A small pond below Asahidake's fuming flank, on the hour-long loop walk from the ropeway's top station.

name: Kurodake (黒岳)
summary: Reached by ropeway and chairlift from Sounkyo and about an hour on foot; the summit looks across Akadake, Hokuchindake and the other peaks of the plateau.

name: Sounkyo Gorge (層雲峡)
summary: A gorge between walls of columnar volcanic rock, with waterfalls and a hot-spring village at its heart.

name: Ginsendai (銀泉台)
summary: A trailhead famous for the earliest autumn colour in Japan, reached by bus from Sounkyo; car access is restricted at the September peak.

name: Daisetsu Kogen Onsen ponds trail (大雪高原温泉沼めぐり登山コース)
summary: A forest circuit of ponds below the Takanegahara ridge, with fumaroles and rare alpine plants. Call at the bear information centre first.

name: Tokachidake (十勝岳)
summary: The active 2,077-metre volcano at the head of the Tokachi range, with many craters. Tokachidake Onsen lies on its slopes; check the alert level.

name: Lake Shikaribetsu (然別湖)
summary: The park's only natural lake, at 810 metres the highest in Hokkaido and about 100 metres deep, home to its own char, the Miyabe iwana.

name: Asahidake Visitor Center
summary: At Asahidake Onsen, built jointly by the Ministry and Higashikawa town: trail conditions and gear hire for Asahidake and Tenninkyo.

name: Sounkyo Visitor Center
summary: The Ministry's centre at Sounkyo Onsen, for Kurodake, Akadake, the Kogen Onsen ponds and the north-east of the range.

name: Higashitaisetsu Nature Center
summary: At Nukabira Gensenkyo on the Tokachi side, covering the eastern mountains, forests and lakes.

name: Poroshiri-dake (幌尻岳)
summary: The highest peak in the range, 2,052 metres, with cirques on its ridges. Sacred to the Ainu, and one of the hardest of Japan's hundred famous mountains.

name: Tokachi-Poroshiri-dake (十勝幌尻岳)
summary: Known locally as Kachi-Poro: a steep climb on a ridge east of the main range, with views over the Tokachi Plain and the whole chain.

name: Mount Apoi (アポイ岳)
summary: A low mountain of mantle peridotite, 810 metres, famous for alpine flowers from late April to October and the centre of the Apoi Geopark.

name: Cape Erimo (襟裳岬)
summary: The range's last ridge running out into the Pacific as a line of reefs. Windy all year; harbour seals rest on the rocks.

name: Lake Toyoni (豊似湖)
summary: A small natural lake in the forest north of Erimo, called the 'heart lake' for its shape from the air.

name: Funbe Falls (フンベの滝)
summary: Spring water pouring off a coastal cliff beside National Route 336, frozen into icicles in winter. Funbe is Ainu for 'whale'.

name: Nissho Pass (日勝峠)
summary: The 1,106-metre pass on National Route 274 between Hidaka and Tokachi, among stone birch and meadow flowers.

name: Saru River source primeval forest (沙流川源流原始林)
summary: A natural monument of Ezo spruce and Sakhalin fir at the head of the Saru River, seen from National Route 274.

name: Hidaka Range Mountain Center
summary: Information centre for the Satsunai River area, with exhibits on the range and its history of mountain accidents. Closed from early November to April.

name: Mount Apoi Geopark Visitor Center
summary: At the foot of Mount Apoi in Samani: the geology, plants and culture of the geopark, and current bear and flower news for the climb.

name: Cape Erimo 'Kaze-no-Yakata'
summary: A wind museum at Cape Erimo with a glass-walled room for watching the seals, and exhibits on kelp and salmon fishing.

name: Lake Shikotsu (支笏湖)
summary: A deep, clear caldera lake ringed by forest and volcanoes, with sightseeing boats, canoes and the ice festival in winter.

name: Tarumae-zan (樽前山)
summary: A volcano south of Lake Shikotsu with a steaming lava dome inside its outer crater rim, and alpine flowers on its upper slopes.

name: Lake Toya and Nakajima (洞爺湖・中島)
summary: A round caldera lake with lava-dome islands at its centre, reached by sightseeing boat; Nakajima has walks of 45 minutes to three hours.

name: Nishiyama and Kompira crater trails (西山火口・金比羅火口散策路)
summary: Footpaths among the craters of Usu's 2000 eruption, past buckled roads and abandoned buildings.

name: Showa-shinzan (昭和新山)
summary: A lava dome pushed up out of a wheat field in 1943–45, now a Special Natural Monument and one of Japan's hundred geological heritage sites.

name: Mount Yotei (羊蹄山)
summary: The 1,898-metre cone of 'Ezo Fuji', climbed by four trails; the Kutchan route and the alpine summit zone are a natural monument.

name: Noboribetsu Jigokudani (登別地獄谷)
summary: An explosion crater about 450 metres long, full of steam vents and boiling pools, and the source of Noboribetsu Onsen's water.

name: Hoheikyo (豊平峡)
summary: A forested gorge above Jozankei, busy in the autumn colour season. The road to the dam is bus-only from May to November.

name: Lake Shikotsu Visitor Center
summary: At Shikotsuko Onsen, with displays and models on the lake and its volcanoes, in a building heated and lit by renewable energy.

name: Toyako Visitor Center and Volcano Science Museum
summary: At Toyako Onsen, on how Usu and the lake were formed, with aerial photographs of the eruptions. The museum charges admission.

name: Toya Takarada Nature Experience House
summary: On Toya's north shore, lending nets, binoculars and winter snowshoes free for the lakeside nature trail.

name: 樽前山七合目ヒュッテ
Lake Towada (十和田湖)
summary: A deep caldera lake with sightseeing boats from Yasumiya, canoe tours, Towada Shrine and the Maidens statue on the south shore.

name: Oirase Gorge (奥入瀬渓流)
summary: Fourteen kilometres of stream, waterfalls and mossy boulders below the lake, with a riverside path the whole way from Nenokuchi to Yakeyama.

name: Hakkoda Ōdake (八甲田大岳)
summary: The highest of the Hakkoda volcanoes, 1,584 metres, reached on foot from Sukayu or the top of the Hakkoda Ropeway. Snow monsters in winter.

name: Tsuta-numa (蔦沼)
summary: A pond in the beech forest near Tsuta Onsen, famous for reflecting red autumn leaves at dawn. Early-morning entry in peak season is booked.

name: Hachimantai and Hachiman-numa (八幡平・八幡沼)
summary: A flat volcanic summit with raised bogs and a crater pond, reached by a short path from the car park on the Aspite Line.

name: Goshogake Onsen (後生掛温泉)
summary: A hot-spring inn with mud baths, next to a nature trail through steaming ground, mud pots and Japan's largest mud volcano.

name: Iwate-san (岩手山)
summary: The park's highest peak, a stratovolcano with a crater-rim path lined with Kannon statues and the bare Yakehashiri lava flow on its flank.

name: Akita-Komagatake (秋田駒ヶ岳)
summary: A group of volcanic peaks topped by Onamedake, 1,637 metres, with meadows of komakusa and other alpine flowers.

name: Towada Visitor Center
summary: At Yasumiya on Lake Towada, explaining the lake's double caldera, with seasonal programmes and crafts.

name: Oirase Keiryūkan
summary: At the lower end of the Oirase Gorge, with a diorama, walking maps and stories of the people drawn to Towada.

name: Sukayu Information Center
summary: Beside Sukayu Onsen, with a relief model of the northern Hakkoda trails. Open late April to early November.

name: Hachimantai Visitor Center
summary: At Goshogake on the Akita side of the Aspite Line, with weather, flower and road reports. Open early April to early November.

name: Matsuo-Hachimantai Visitor Center
summary: The information centre for the Iwate side of Hachimantai, with a film theatre of the four seasons.

name: Amihari Visitor Center
summary: At Amihari Onsen below Iwate-san, the park's highest peak, with guided programmes.

name: Tanesashi Coast (種差海岸)
summary: Natural lawn running right down to the sea, shaped by horse grazing since long ago, with a coastal path past flowers that mix beach and mountain species.

name: Kabushima (蕪島)
summary: A small hill at Hachinohe crowned by a shrine to Benzaiten, where tens of thousands of black-tailed gulls nest from March. The trail's northern start.

name: Kitayamazaki (北山崎)
summary: Two-hundred-metre cliffs, headlands and sea caves, the most famous view on the coast. Clifftop paths, and tours in small fishing boats called sappa.

name: Jodogahama (浄土ヶ浜)
summary: A cove of sharp white rocks, pines and deep blue water near Miyako, with a summer swimming beach and boats into the sea caves.

name: Goishi Coast and Anatōshi-iso (碁石海岸・穴通磯)
summary: Sawtooth cliffs near Ōfunato and a sea rock pierced by three large holes, which small boats can pass through.

name: Miracle Pine (奇跡の一本松)
summary: At Rikuzentakata, the one pine left standing when the 2011 tsunami swept away the Takata Matsubara forest, preserved as a monument after it died.

name: Ogama-Hanzō (巨釜半造)
summary: Limestone coast on the Karakuwa Peninsula with Oreishi, a sixteen-metre pillar whose top was broken off by the 1896 tsunami.

name: Kinkasan (金華山)
summary: A sacred, wooded island off the Oshika Peninsula, where deer, held to be messengers of the gods, roam freely.

name: Tanesashi Coast Information Center
summary: On the Tanesashi lawn: nature and culture of the Tanesashi coast, hands-on programmes and trail information.

name: Kitayamazaki Visitor Center
summary: At the Kitayamazaki observatories, with a free film of the cliffs through the seasons and wildlife exhibits.

name: Jodogahama Visitor Center
summary: The park's main centre, with information on the whole coast and news from each area.

name: Goishi Coast Information Center
summary: At the Goishi Coast near Ōfunato, with nature programmes and information on the Michinoku Coastal Trail.

name: Karakuwa Peninsula Visitor Center
summary: On the Karakuwa Peninsula near Kesennuma, with exhibits on the earthquake and tsunami.

name: Minamisanriku Marine Visitor Center
summary: On Shizugawa Bay, the base for exploring the Ramsar bay and its eelgrass and seaweed beds.

name: Ishinomaki Kawa no Visitor Center
summary: Near the mouth of the Kitakami River in Ishinomaki, the river-themed partner of the Minamisanriku centre.

name: Oshika Peninsula Visitor Center
summary: At the tip of the Oshika Peninsula, facing Kinkasan.

name: Goshikinuma (五色沼)
summary: A cluster of ponds left by the 1888 eruption, each a different blue, green or rust; a path of about four kilometres links them from the Urabandai Visitor Center.

name: Mount Bandai (磐梯山)
summary: A volcano whose 1888 eruption tore away its north side. Trails climb to the top, past the raw scar of the collapse above Urabandai.

name: Jododaira and the Witch's Eye (浄土平・魔女の瞳)
summary: A volcanic plateau at about 1,600 metres on the Bandai-Azuma Skyline, with trails up Issaikyō-zan to view the cobalt crater lake.

name: Lake Inawashiro (猪苗代湖)
summary: Japan's fourth-largest lake, called the 'sky mirror'. Tundra swans winter on it, and spray freezes on the shore in deep winter.

name: Ogunuma (雄国沼)
summary: A high wetland west of Bandai, a natural monument, carpeted with Nikkō-kisuge daylilies from mid-June to early July.

name: Mount Haguro (羽黒山)
summary: The first of the Dewa Sanzan, climbed through an avenue of giant cedars past a National Treasure five-storey pagoda.

name: Ōasahi-dake (大朝日岳)
summary: The 1,870-metre high point of the Asahi range, usually climbed as part of a traverse of two or three nights or more.

name: Iide-san (飯豊山)
summary: The 2,105-metre main peak of the Iide range, with a shrine on top and flower meadows along gentle ridges at the end of hard approaches.

name: Urabandai Visitor Center
summary: On the Goshikinuma path in Urabandai, with information on nature, culture and current trail conditions.

name: Jododaira Visitor Center
summary: At Jododaira on the Bandai-Azuma Skyline, for the Azuma volcanoes. Closed from mid-November to early April with the road.

name: Mount Gassan Visitor Center
summary: At Mount Haguro, with displays on the nature and climate of Dewa Sanzan.

name: Yamagata Prefectural Nature Museum
summary: In the beech forest on Gassan's eastern side at Nishikawa, with trails for watching plants and birds.

name: Tōshō-gū and the Shrines and Temples of Nikkō
summary: Tōshō-gū, Futarasan Shrine and Rinnō-ji: 103 buildings in cedar forest above the town, including the carved Yōmeimon gate. A World Heritage Site.

name: Kegon Falls
summary: 華厳滝 Kegon-no-taki: the outflow of Lake Chūzenji drops 97 metres over the edge of an old lava flow.

name: Lake Chūzenji
summary: A lake dammed by Mount Nantai's lava about 20,000 years ago, with the former British and Italian embassy villas on its shore.

name: Senjōgahara
summary: A former lake turned high moor, crossed by a boardwalk nature trail beside the Yu River, with Mount Nantai on the skyline.

name: Mount Nantai
summary: The sacred 2,486-metre volcano above Lake Chūzenji, climbed from the gate of Futarasan Shrine's Chūgūshi in the climbing season.

name: Mount Nikkō-Shirane
summary: The highest peak in Kantō, at 2,578 metres; climbed from Yumoto, Lake Suganuma or the top of the Marunuma ropeway.

name: Nasu-dake (Chausu-dake)
summary: The steaming 1,915-metre main peak of the Nasu range, an active volcano reached on foot from the top of the Nasu Ropeway.

name: Sesshō-seki
summary: 殺生石, the 'killing stone' of legend, among volcanic gas vents at Nasu Yumoto. It was found split in two in March 2022.

name: Nikko Yumoto Visitor Center
summary: The Ministry's centre at Yumoto Onsen: trail and wildlife news for Oku-Nikkō, nature walks, and snowshoe hire in winter.

name: Tochigi Prefectural Nikko Natural Science Museum
summary: Beside Kegon Falls on Lake Chūzenji: exhibits on Oku-Nikkō's nature and current conditions. Admission is charged.

name: Nasu Heisei-no-Mori Field Centre
summary: Base for guided walks in the forest opened in 2011 on former imperial villa land.

name: Shiobara Onsen Visitor Center
summary: Information for the walks along the Hōki River gorge and its waterfalls at Shiobara.

name: Ozegahara
summary: 尾瀬ヶ原: one of Japan's largest mountain marshes, about 1,400 metres up between Shibutsu and Hiuchigatake, crossed by double boardwalks.

name: Ozenuma
summary: 尾瀬沼: a lake about 1,665 metres up, dammed by Hiuchigatake's eruptions, with marshes and the visitor centre on its eastern shore.

name: Mount Hiuchigatake
summary: 燧ヶ岳: at 2,356 metres the highest mountain in Tōhoku, a volcano last active in 1544. Climbed from Miike, Ozenuma or Miharashi.

name: Mount Shibutsu
summary: 至仏山: a 2,228-metre peak of serpentinite with rare plants. Closed in the snowmelt season; the trail from Yamanohana is for ascent only.

name: Sanjō Falls
summary: 三条の滝: the Tadami River, carrying all of Ozegahara's water, falls about 100 metres. A long walk from Miharashi or Miike.

name: Ayamedaira
summary: A high marsh south of Ozegahara, trampled bare in the 1960s and being replanted since 1966. Quieter than the main marsh.

name: Mount Aizu-Komagatake
summary: 会津駒ヶ岳: a 2,133-metre peak in the north of the park, its broad summit ridge dotted with pools. Added to the park in 2007.

name: Ozenuma Visitor Center
summary: On the east shore of Ozenuma: exhibits, current trail and flower news, and daily guided nature walks in season.

name: Oze Yamanohana Visitor Center
summary: At Yamanohana, the western edge of Ozegahara, about an hour's walk from Hatomachi Pass.

name: Mount Kimpu (金峰山)
summary: The 2,599-metre crown of the range and its only summit above the tree line, with creeping pine and a clear view south to Mount Fuji.

name: Nishizawa Gorge (西沢渓谷)
summary: A loop through old forest past waterfall after waterfall to Nanatsugama Godan-no-taki, a five-tiered fall named among Japan's hundred finest.

name: Mitake-Shōsenkyō (御岳昇仙峡)
summary: A granite gorge north of Kōfu, a Special Place of Scenic Beauty, ending at Sengataki Falls. A ropeway climbs to a lookout with Mount Fuji on clear days.

name: Mount Kumotori (雲取山)
summary: Tokyo's highest summit, 2,017 metres, where Tokyo, Saitama and Yamanashi meet. Long trails climb it from Kamozawa on the Okutama side and from Mitsumine Shrine.

name: Mount Mitake (御岳山)
summary: A 929-metre sacred mountain reached by cable car, with a village of pilgrim lodgings around Musashi-Mitake Shrine and waterfall trails beyond.

name: Mitsumine Shrine (三峯神社)
summary: A mountain shrine in the Chichibu hills where wolves stand guard in stone, and the start of the long ridge walk to Kumotori.

name: Daibosatsu Pass (大菩薩峠)
summary: A 1,897-metre saddle on an open grassy ridge below Daibosatsu-rei, looking over the Kōfu basin to the Southern Alps and Mount Fuji.

name: Mitake Valley (御岳渓谷)
summary: The clear upper Tama River near Mitake Station, with riverside paths on both banks and white water used for rafting and kayaking.

name: Mitake Visitor Center
summary: Exhibits and trail information on Mount Mitake's nature, culture and walking routes.

name: Okutama Visitor Center
summary: Two minutes' walk from Okutama Station: maps, trail conditions and exhibits for the Okutama mountains.

name: Yama-no-Furusato-mura Visitor Center
summary: In a Tokyo metropolitan park on the south shore of Lake Okutama, with nature programmes, a campsite and cabins.

name: Mitsumine Visitor Center
summary: Near Mitsumine Shrine: exhibits on the park's wildlife and on how its mountains and valleys formed.

name: Minamijima (南島)
summary: A drowned-karst islet off Chichijima, with the white cove of Ōgi-ike inside a rock arch. Landing only with a Tokyo-certified guide; closed for about three months from November.

name: Weather Station Observatory
summary: A lookout on Chichijima's west side, crowded at sunset when the sun drops into the open sea, and a good place to watch for humpback whales in season.

name: Chihiroiwa — Heart Rock (千尋岩)
summary: A sea cliff on Chichijima's south coast stained red in a heart shape by laterite soil washed down from above, reached on guided treks.

name: Anijima Marine Park (兄島海域公園)
summary: Very clear water off Anijima's south shore, with coral and shoals of reef fish, visited on snorkelling and sea-kayak tours.

name: Miyanohama (宮之浜)
summary: A beach within walking distance of town, with coral and tropical fish. Currents run fast beyond the bay; swim inside the buoys.

name: Higashidaira Sanctuary (東平)
summary: Twenty-eight hectares of Chichijima forest kept for the red-headed wood pigeon and other rare species; walked only with a trained guide or after the Forestry Agency's course.

name: Mount Chibusa (乳房山)
summary: At 462 metres the highest point on the inhabited islands: a cloud forest of tree ferns and endemic land snails, with a view over all Hahajima.

name: Minamizaki (南崎)
summary: Hahajima's southern tip, through fan-palm and pandanus woods to a coral beach; the path climbs Kofuji for a view over the southern islets.

name: Ogasawara Visitor Center
summary: Panels, reconstructed models and films on the islands' nature, history and culture, on Chichijima.

name: Ogasawara World Heritage Centre
summary: Explains the work to protect the heritage site, breeds endangered species where visitors can watch, and houses the Ministry of the Environment's ranger office.

name: Ogasawara Village Tourist Association
summary: In the B-Ship building by Futami Port: the first stop for Chichijima's tours, guides, maps and lodging.

name: Ogasawara Hahajima Tourist Association
summary: Hahajima's information centre: tours, maps and lodging on the island.

name: Mount Fuji (富士山)
summary: Japan's highest mountain at 3,776 m, last in eruption in 1707. Four trails climb from the fifth stations in a season of about ten weeks each summer.

name: Ōwakudani (大涌谷)
summary: A valley of steaming vents left by an eruption about 3,000 years ago, crossed by the Hakone Ropeway. Access depends on volcanic activity and gas.

name: Lake Ashi (芦ノ湖)
summary: Hakone's caldera lake, crossed by sightseeing boats, with Hakone Shrine and the old Tōkaidō highway at Moto-Hakone on its south-east shore.

name: Lake Motosu (本栖湖)
summary: The deepest of the Fuji Five Lakes. Its reflected view of Fuji is the one printed on the back of the ¥1,000 note issued from 2004.

name: Aokigahara and Fugaku Fuketsu (青木ヶ原・富岳風穴)
summary: Forest grown on the lava of the 864 Jōgan eruption. Fugaku Fuketsu, a lava tube in the forest, stays around 3°C in midsummer.

name: Shiraito Falls (白糸の滝)
summary: Groundwater from Fuji spills from between lava layers in hundreds of threads down a curved cliff about 20 m high. Part of the World Heritage site.

name: Jōgasaki Coast (城ヶ崎海岸)
summary: About 9 km of black lava cliffs, left when Ōmuroyama's lava ran into the sea some 4,000 years ago.

name: Mount Mihara (三原山), Izu Ōshima
summary: Izu Ōshima's active volcano, watched around the clock by the Japan Meteorological Agency. Its 1986 eruption sent about 11,000 islanders off the island for a month.

name: Yamanashi Prefectural Mt. Fuji World Heritage Center (山梨県立富士山世界遺産センター)
summary: Yamanashi Prefecture's centre for the north side of Fuji, at Funatsu in Fujikawaguchiko; its north building is the former Fuji Visitor Center.

name: Lake Tanuki Nature School (田貫湖ふれあい自然塾)
summary: The Ministry of the Environment's first nature school, on Lake Tanuki below Fuji's western face, with programmes and cottages.

name: Hakone Visitor Center (箱根ビジターセンター)
summary: The Ministry of the Environment's centre for Hakone, near the north shore of Lake Ashi. Maps, trail advice and help in English.

name: Kitadake (北岳)
summary: Japan's second-highest peak at 3,193 m, and with Ainodake and Nōtoridake the Shirane Sanzan. Its east face falls 600 m as the Kitadake Buttress.

name: Senjōgatake (仙丈ヶ岳)
summary: The 'Queen of the Minami Alps', 3,033 m: a broad, gentle mountain with glacial cirques, among the easiest of the high peaks from Kitazawa Pass.

name: Kaikomagatake (甲斐駒ヶ岳)
summary: A pale granite peak of 2,967 m, sacred since the 1800s. The Kuroto ridge route passes stone monuments and statues left by generations of pilgrims.

name: Hōō Sanzan (鳳凰三山)
summary: Yakushidake, Kannondake and Jizōdake: granite summits around 2,800 m with white granite slopes, and a saddle crowded with small stone Jizō statues below Jizōdake.

name: Ainodake (間ノ岳)
summary: A massive 3,190 m summit at the source of the Ōi River, with the Kitazawa and Hosozawa cirques on its flanks.

name: Shiomidake (塩見岳)
summary: A twin-topped dome at the south end of the long Senshō ridge: the east peak is higher, 3,052 m, the west peak carries the survey point.

name: Arakawa Sanzan (荒川三山)
summary: Warusawadake, Nakadake and Maedake, over 3,000 m: the southernmost clear glacial landforms in Japan, and flower meadows on Maedake's south-east slope.

name: Akaishidake (赤石岳)
summary: A broad 3,121 m peak with Japan's highest first-order survey point. The whole Akaishi range takes its name from it.

name: Norogawa-Hirogawara Information Centre
summary: Above the bus and taxi terminal at Hirogawara, the Kitadake trailhead: trail and weather information, and a police post in summer. Closed mid-November to early June.

name: Ashiyasu Mountain Museum (芦安山岳館)
summary: Exhibits on the range's nature, history and climbing, with a mountain library, near the Ashiyasu bus stop for Hirogawara. Admission charged.

name: Minami Alps Hase Visitor Center
summary: Outdoor and tourist information beside the Minami Alps-mura Hase roadside station, on the Nagano approach to Kitazawa Pass.

name: Minami Alps Shizen Fureai Centre
summary: Trail and weather information at Sawarajima Lodge, the southern trailhead in Shizuoka. Closed December to April.

name: Yugama (湯釜), Kusatsu-Shirane
summary: An acid, milky-green crater lake in a bare volcanic bowl. Access to the rim depends on the volcanic alert level; check before you go.

name: Onioshidashi (鬼押出し)
summary: A field of black lava blocks left by Asama's 1783 eruption, with paths through it and the volcano rising behind.

name: Jigokudani Yaen-kōen (地獄谷野猿公苑)
summary: Wild Japanese macaques bathing in a hot spring in the Yokoyu valley, reached by a 2 km forest path.

name: Yonjūhachi-ike (四十八池), Shiga Kogen
summary: A high moor at about 1,880 m scattered with dozens of small ponds, among the lava-plateau wetlands of Shiga Kogen.

name: Ichinokura-sawa (一ノ倉沢)
summary: A valley head below Tanigawa-dake's sheer rock walls, where most of the mountain's climbing accidents have happened. A place to look up from unless you are an expert.

name: Yoshigadaira wetlands (芳ヶ平湿地群)
summary: Ramsar-listed volcanic bogs and ponds on the flank of Kusatsu-Shirane.

name: Naeba-san (苗場山)
summary: A flat lava summit at 2,145 m covered by a broad high moor.

name: Yonako Falls (米子大瀑布)
summary: Twin waterfalls, Fudō-daki and Gongen-daki, above Suzaka; long a place of Shugendō practice, where ascetics still bathe under the falls in summer.

name: Shiga Kogen Nature Conservation Centre (志賀高原自然保護センター)
summary: In the Shiga Kogen Sōgō Kaikan 98 at Hasuike: models and panels on the plateau's forests, moors and people, with a guides' association alongside. Open all year.

name: Tanigawa-dake Information Centre (谷川岳インフォメーションセンター)
summary: At Doai, by the Tanigawa-dake Ropeway: geology, wildlife and route exhibits, and current flower and trail news.

name: Manza Nature Information Centre (万座しぜん情報館)
summary: At Manza Onsen: displays, seasonal guided walks, a small amphibian aquarium and a terrace over the fumaroles of Karabuki.

name: Asama North Foot Visitor Center (浅間山北麓ビジターセンター)
summary: At Asama-en on the volcano's north foot: a diorama of how Asama formed and its plants changed, rocks and Geopark displays. Fridays to Sundays only from December to March.

name: Myōkō-san (妙高山)
summary: The park's signature volcano, 2,454 m: a lava dome inside the rim of an older crater. Trails climb from Tsubame, Seki and Akakura onsen and from Sasagamine.

name: Tengu-no-niwa and Kōya-ike (天狗の庭・高谷池)
summary: High moor and pools below Mount Hiuchi, with a mountain hut at Kōya-ike. Autumn colour peaks in the second half of September.

name: Togakushi Shrine (戸隠神社)
summary: Five shrines joined by old paths. The walk to Okusha passes a thatched gate and an avenue of cedars about 400 years old.

name: Kagami-ike (鏡池)
summary: A still pond in the forest that mirrors the jagged Togakushi range.

name: Lake Nojiri (野尻湖)
summary: A lake below Kurohime and Myōkō for canoeing, sailing and paddleboarding; Naumann's elephant fossils have come from its bed.

name: Imori-ike (いもり池)
summary: A pond at Myōkō Kōgen with the mountain reflected in it, beside the visitor centre.

name: Naena Falls (苗名滝)
summary: A 55 m waterfall on the upper Seki river, called jishin-daki, the earthquake falls, for its roar.

name: Kamaike (鎌池)
summary: A pond in beech forest at the foot of Mount Amakazari, with a path around it.

name: Myōkō Kōgen Visitor Center (妙高高原ビジターセンター)
summary: Beside Imori-ike: the area's wildlife, plants and culture, and current trail news.

name: 82 Mori-no-Manabiya Forest Learning Centre
summary: At the Togakushi Forest Botanical Garden: the forest's plants and birds, with guided walks on Sundays from May to October. Closed from December to late April.

name: Nojiri-ko Naumann Elephant Museum (野尻湖ナウマンゾウ博物館)
summary: Fossils and finds from the lake bed, including Naumann's elephant and Yabe's giant deer.

name: Kamikochi and Kappa-bashi (上高地・河童橋)
summary: A level valley floor at about 1,500 metres on the Azusa River, where the suspension bridge looks up to the Hotaka peaks. Reached only by bus or taxi.

name: Murodō and Mikurigaike (室堂・みくりが池)
summary: The Alpine Route's highest stop at 2,450 metres, beside a blue crater lake, with paths up Oyama and towards the fumaroles of Jigokudani.

name: Yarigatake (槍ヶ岳)
summary: The spear-shaped 3,180-metre summit at the head of the Azusa, first climbed by the priest Banryū in 1828.

name: Karasawa cirque and the Hotaka peaks (涸沢・穂高連峰)
summary: A glacial cirque under Okuhotakadake, at 3,190 metres the joint third-highest mountain in Japan. Famous for autumn colour.

name: Taishō-ike (大正池)
summary: The pond made in 1915 when an eruption of Yakedake dammed the Azusa River; the volcano, still active, rises behind it.

name: Mount Norikura (乗鞍岳)
summary: The park's southern volcano. Buses climb to Tatamidaira at 2,702 metres, among alpine flowers below the 3,026-metre summit, Kengamine.

name: Hakuba Daisekkei (白馬大雪渓)
summary: One of Japan's three great snow gullies, climbed on snow on the way up Shiroumadake (2,932 metres).

name: Shōmyō Falls (称名滝)
summary: Japan's highest waterfall: 350 metres in four drops off the edge of the Midagahara plateau.

name: Kamikochi Visitor Center
summary: The Ministry of the Environment's centre near Kappa-bashi: trail conditions, bear sightings, nature walks. Open late April to 15 November.

name: Kamikochi Information Centre
summary: At the Kamikochi bus terminal: maps, weather and transport information. Open late April to 15 November.

name: Tateyama Nature Conservation Centre
summary: Toyama Prefecture's centre at Murodō on the area's nature. Open mid-April to mid-November.

name: Keyakidaira Visitor Center
summary: At the end of the Kurobe Gorge Railway, with trail conditions and films on the gorge. Open while the railway runs.

name: 東京大学運動会乗鞍寮
Gozengamine (御前峰)
summary: Hakusan's highest summit, 2,702 metres, with the Okumiya, the inner shrine of Shirayama-hime Shrine.

name: Midorigaike and the crater ponds (翠ヶ池)
summary: Crater lakes north of the summit, on the Oike-meguri loop of about two hours from Murodō past the summit ponds.

name: Minami-Ryūgababa (南竜ヶ馬場)
summary: A meadow in the saddle between Hakusan and Bessan, with boardwalks through Hakusan primroses, a hut, cabins and a campground.

name: Ubagataki (姥ヶ滝)
summary: A broad waterfall in the Jadani gorge, seen from the Oyadani no Yu foot bath off the White Road. The path has been closed by rockfall; check before you go.

name: Fukube Great Waterfall (ふくべの大滝)
summary: An 86-metre fall right beside the White Road, one of seven along the road on the Ishikawa side.

name: Shiramizu Falls (白水滝)
summary: On the Gifu side, a single fall of milky-white water dropping through forest in the Ōshirakawa valley, near the start of the Hirase trail.

name: Itoshiro Great Cedar (石徹白のスギ)
summary: A Japanese cedar thought to be about 1,800 years old, on the old Mino pilgrim route; a Special Natural Monument.

name: Ichinose Visitor Center
summary: Run by Ishikawa Prefecture's Hakusan Nature Conservation Centre, at the Ichinose car park and shuttle-bus stop. Open 29 April to 5 November.

name: Hakusan Murodō Visitor Center
summary: Beside the large mountain hut at Murodō, below Gozengamine, for trail and weather information.

name: Chūgū Onsen Visitor Center
summary: Ishikawa Prefecture's centre at Chūgū on the White Road, with exhibits on the park's nature and history. Open late April to mid-November.

name: Ise Jingū Inner Shrine (内宮 Naikū)
summary: Amaterasu's shrine, reached over the Uji Bridge and through centuries-old trees beside the Isuzu River. Its sanctuary has been rebuilt every twenty years since 690.

name: Yokoyama Observatory (横山展望台)
summary: Ago Bay from above: a maze of drowned valleys, wooded islets and rows of pearl rafts. The park's visitor centre is close by.

name: Meoto Iwa, Futami-ura (夫婦岩)
summary: Two sea rocks off Futami's old purification beach, tied together by a sacred rope, with a torii on the larger. From May to July the sun rises between them.

name: Mount Asama (朝熊ヶ岳)
summary: The park's highest point at 555 m. The summit observatory looks across Ise Bay and down the Shima coast, and on clear winter days to Mount Fuji.

name: Daiōzaki Lighthouse (大王埼灯台)
summary: A lighthouse on the cape above the fishing town of Daiō, where the Kinki Nature Trail turns from the sheltered bays to the open Pacific.

name: Anorisaki Lighthouse (安乗埼灯台)
summary: Climb it for the open Pacific on one side and a calm bay on the other. One of Japan's fifty selected lighthouses.

name: Mieshima Viewpoint, Ugura Park (見江島展望台)
summary: Over the drowned valleys of the Minami-Ise coast to a heart-shaped inlet, with tuna and pearl farms in the water below.

name: Kamishima (神島)
summary: The farthest of Toba's four inhabited islands, under one square kilometre, with white limestone karst by the sea. The setting of Yukio Mishima's novel The Sound of Waves.

name: Yokoyama Visitor Center (横山ビジターセンター)
summary: The Ministry of the Environment's centre above Ago Bay, beside the Yokoyama Observatory: exhibits on the park's plants and animals, and nature programmes. Usually closed Tuesdays; check ahead.

name: Toba Visitor Center (鳥羽ビジターセンター)
summary: The park's general desk for outdoor activities in Toba, with current information and staff to answer visitors' questions.

name: Nachi Falls (那智滝)
summary: A single drop of 133 metres, Japan's tallest, worshipped as a deity by the Kumano Nachi shrine. Approach by the cedar-lined stone steps of Daimonzaka.

name: Ōdaigahara (大台ヶ原)
summary: High plateau of beech, spruce and dwarf bamboo. Trails from the car park lead to Hidegatake (1,695 m), the highest point in Mie, and the rock outcrop of Daijagura.

name: Mount Yoshino (吉野山)
summary: A ridge of temples covered with thousands of cherry trees, Japan's best-known blossom hill in early spring, and the northern end of the Ōmine pilgrimage.

name: Hakkyōgatake (八経ヶ岳)
summary: At 1,915 metres the highest peak in Kansai, on the Ōmine Okugake ascetic route. A long, steep mountain walk.

name: Dorokyō Gorge (瀞峡)
summary: The Kitayama River runs green between sheer rock walls; Doro-hatchō is the best-known stretch. The gorge's jet boats were suspended in 2021 and withdrawn in 2025.

name: Hashiguiiwa (橋杭岩)
summary: A line of rock pillars striding out from the shore at Kushimoto — 'bridge-pile rocks', like the piers of an unfinished bridge.

name: Cape Shionomisaki (潮岬)
summary: The southern tip of Honshu, a headland looking out over the Kuroshio current.

name: Senjōjiki (千畳敷)
summary: Broad, wave-cut terraces of layered sandstone and mudstone on the Shirahama coast.

name: Ōdaigahara Visitor Center
summary: At the plateau car park: trail conditions, maps, and the compulsory lecture for Nishi-Ōdai.

name: Ugui Visitor Center
summary: Visitor centre on the Ugui peninsula in Nachikatsuura, for the Kumano coast.

name: Nanki Kumano Geopark Center
summary: On Cape Shionomisaki: how the peninsula's rocks, coast and coral seas came to be.

name: Tottori Sand Dunes (鳥取砂丘)
summary: Rolling dunes of sand from the Sendai River, a natural monument. Walk, sandboard or paraglide; the wind redraws the ripples daily.

name: Uradome Coast (浦富海岸)
summary: Granite headlands, pine-topped islets such as Senganmatsushima, sea caves and the quartz-sand coves of Kamogaiso. Best by sightseeing boat or sea kayak.

name: Tajima Mihonoura (但馬御火浦)
summary: Eight kilometres of cliffs, sea caves and arches, including the huge Tsurigane Dōmon, and the column-jointed islet of Mio-Ōshima. A scenic place and natural monument.

name: Yoroi-no-sode (鎧の袖)
summary: A sea cliff of jointed columns 65 metres high and 200 metres long, named for the sleeve of samurai armour it resembles.

name: Takenohama and Nekozaki (竹野浜・猫崎)
summary: A white-sand beach beside a cat-shaped peninsula; the snorkelling centre here leads trips over the reefs.

name: Genbudō (玄武洞)
summary: Hexagonal basalt columns where Motonori Matuyama found evidence of reversals of Earth's magnetic field in 1926. A natural monument beside the Maruyama River.

name: Shōtenkyō and Kumihama Bay (小天橋・久美浜湾)
summary: A pine-covered sandbar that all but seals Kumihama Bay from the Sea of Japan, at the park's eastern end.

name: Tottori Sand Dunes Visitor Center
summary: Dune ecology, weather and the day's conditions, at the edge of the dunes.

name: Takeno Snorkeling Center
summary: Snorkelling lessons, gear and guided trips at Takenohama.

name: Itsukushima and Mount Misen (厳島・弥山)
summary: Miyajima's shrine and its torii standing in the tide, with trails and a ropeway up Mount Misen behind. A World Heritage Site; stay overnight to see it quiet.

name: Naruto Strait (鳴門海峡)
summary: Tidal whirlpools between Awaji Island and Shikoku, formed as the tide races through the narrow strait. Sightseeing boats run out to them.

name: Washūzan (鷲羽山)
summary: A granite hill at the tip of the Kojima Peninsula, one of the park's original viewpoints, looking over the islands of the Bisan Seto and the Seto Ōhashi bridges.

name: Kankakei (寒霞渓)
summary: A rocky gorge in the mountains of Shōdoshima; one of the original 1934 sites.

name: Yashima (屋島)
summary: A flat-topped hill above Takamatsu with views over the islands; one of the original 1934 sites.

name: Tomonoura and Sensuijima (鞆の浦・仙酔島)
summary: A historic port where ships once waited for the tide, and the wild island just offshore with coloured volcanic rocks and a beach.

name: Mount Rokkō (六甲山)
summary: The granite range behind Kobe; its 931-metre summit looks over the city, Osaka Bay and the sea.

name: Shimanami Kaidō (しまなみ海道)
summary: A 70-kilometre cycle route over six islands between Onomichi and Imabari. From Kirōsan on Ōshima, look down on the Kurushima Strait, where tides reach about 10 knots.

name: Goshikidai Visitor Center
summary: On the Goshikidai uplands between Takamatsu and Sakaide, looking over the Bisan Seto.

name: Ōkunoshima Visitor Center
summary: On Ōkunoshima, a small island off Takehara in Hiroshima Prefecture.

name: Mount Daisen (大山)
summary: The highest peak in Chūgoku, 1,729 metres. The trail from Daisen-ji climbs through beech forest to the 1,709-metre Misen summit in about three hours.

name: Hiruzen Highlands (蒜山高原)
summary: Three rounded peaks over a broad upland on the Okayama–Tottori border, cool in summer, with camping, hiking and horse riding.

name: Mitokusan and Nageire-dō (三徳山・投入堂)
summary: A pilgrims' scramble up roots and rock to a temple hall built into a cliff, a National Treasure. No solo climbers; closed in winter.

name: Mount Sanbe (三瓶山)
summary: Lava domes ringed round a caldera, with ponds on the uplands and wide views from the 1,126-metre summit of Osanbe.

name: Izumo Taisha (出雲大社)
summary: One of Japan's oldest and grandest shrines, whose god is said to have made the land. Inside the park at the foot of the Shimane Peninsula.

name: Hinomisaki (日御碕)
summary: The western tip of the Shimane Peninsula, a lighthouse on the cliffs above the Sea of Japan.

name: Kuniga Coast and Matengai (国賀海岸・摩天崖)
summary: Nishinoshima's sea cliffs, arches and stacks; Matengai drops more than 250 metres to the sea. Walk the cliff-top pasture or take a boat.

name: Jōdogaura (浄土ヶ浦)
summary: A cove of small islands, caves and pines on the east coast of Dōgo, the largest Oki island; a national scenic place.

name: Daisen Museum of Nature and History
summary: The mountain's nature and history, in the village below Daisen-ji.

name: Sahimel — Shimane Nature Museum of Mount Sanbe
summary: Natural history museum at the foot of Mount Sanbe.

name: Oki Nature Museum
summary: The islands' geology and wildlife, by the port of Saigō on Dōgo.

name: Cape Ashizuri (足摺岬)
summary: Granite cliffs at the southern tip of Shikoku, with a lighthouse first lit in 1914 and the pilgrim temple Kongōfukuji close by. The sea below is the Kuroshio.

name: Hakusan Dōmon (白山洞門)
summary: A great natural arch of granite near the cape, said to be the largest granite cave in Japan.

name: Tatsukushi (竜串)
summary: Sandstone shore weathered into strange shapes. Glass-bottomed boats and an undersea observatory show the coral of the marine park.

name: Minokoshi (見残し)
summary: More wave-sculpted sandstone near Tatsukushi; the name means 'left unseen'.

name: Kashiwajima (柏島)
summary: A small island ringed by famously clear water, a centre for diving and snorkelling.

name: Okinoshima (沖の島)
summary: An island reached by ferry, surrounded by marine park zones, with a great variety of fish in its warm water.

name: Nametoko Ravine (滑床渓谷)
summary: The Meguro River slides over smooth granite for some 12 kilometres; Yukiwa Falls glides about 80 metres down a single slab. Walking trails and summer canyoning.

name: Tatsukushi Visitor Center Uminowa (竜串ビジターセンター うみのわ)
summary: The park's visitor centre on the Tatsukushi coast: exhibits, conditions and the local diving, snorkelling and boat tours.

name: Kujūkushima (九十九島)
summary: Officially 208 islands, in a maze of sheltered water off Sasebo. Cruise or kayak from the Pearl Sea Resort at Kashimae.

name: Tenkaihō (展海峰)
summary: A hilltop viewpoint looking out across the Kujūkushima islands.

name: Ōbae Lighthouse, Ikitsuki (大バエ灯台)
summary: On the northernmost point of Ikitsuki, with a viewing platform and wide views over the open sea.

name: Nozakijima (野崎島)
summary: An almost abandoned island off Ojika, reached by ferry, where deer graze around the old Nokubi church.

name: Ōsezaki Cliffs and Lighthouse (大瀬崎)
summary: Sea cliffs at Fukue's south-western tip, the westernmost point of the Gotō Islands; in autumn, honey buzzards pass overhead on migration.

name: Takahama Beach (高浜)
summary: White sand and glassy water in a sheltered bay on Fukue, beside neighbouring Tonmarihama.

name: Mount Onidake (鬼岳)
summary: A grass-covered cinder cone above Fukue town, with a large crater and wide views over the islands.

name: Kujūkushima Visitor Center
summary: At the Pearl Sea Resort in Kashimae, Sasebo: the islands' nature, boat trips and kayaking.

name: Abunze Visitor Center (鐙瀬ビジターセンター)
summary: On Fukue's Abunze lava coast below Mount Onidake: the Gotō Islands' nature and trails.

name: Mount Fugen and Heisei Shinzan (普賢岳・平成新山)
summary: Climb from Nita Pass to Fugendake's 1,359-metre summit for a close view of the lava dome of 1990–95, the park's newest and highest peak.

name: Nita Pass (仁田峠)
summary: Trailheads, a ropeway up towards Myōkendake and views over the volcano. Azaleas in May and colour in autumn.

name: Unzen Jigoku (雲仙地獄)
summary: The 'hells' at Unzen Onsen: boardwalks over steaming, sulphurous vents and bubbling pools in the middle of the hot-spring town.

name: Mount Takabuto and Amakusa Matsushima (高舞登山・天草松島)
summary: A hilltop lookout over the islets of Amakusa Matsushima, best at sunset.

name: Jūsanbutsu Park (十三仏公園)
summary: A clifftop view over Myōkenura, a scenic place and natural monument on Shimoshima's west coast: sea cliffs, sea caves and an elephant-shaped rock.

name: Heisei Shinzan Nature Center
summary: Close to the lava dome on its eastern side, with the story of the 1990–95 eruption.

name: Amakusa Visitor Center
summary: On Kamishima near Mount Takabuto, introducing the islands, their sea and their walks.

name: Unzen Suwanoike Visitor Center (雲仙諏訪の池ビジターセンター)
summary: By the Suwa ponds on the volcano's south-western slopes.

name: Tomioka Visitor Center (富岡ビジターセンター)
summary: On the Tomioka peninsula at the north-west tip of Shimoshima, Amakusa.

name: Nakadake Crater (中岳火口)
summary: Aso's active crater, with a steaming lake of pale green water. Reached from the Aso-sanjō terminal by the crater shuttle or the toll road when the crater is open.

name: Kusasenri (草千里ヶ浜)
summary: A broad grassy meadow with a pond among Aso's central peaks; horse riding.

name: Komezuka (米塚)
summary: A small, almost perfectly shaped volcanic cone about 80 metres high on the slopes above the caldera floor.

name: Daikanbō (大観峰)
summary: A lookout on the northern caldera rim, over the farmed caldera floor to the five peaks of Aso.

name: Kujūsan (久住山)
summary: The Kujū range's namesake peak, 1,786 metres, climbed from Makinoto Pass; Nakadake, the Kyushu mainland's highest, is a short walk on.

name: Tadewara Marsh (タデ原)
summary: A Ramsar-listed highland marsh with a walking trail, beside the Chōjabaru Visitor Center.

name: Bōgatsuru (坊ガツル)
summary: A high marshy basin among the Kujū peaks, part of the Ramsar site, reached only on foot.

name: Mount Yufu (由布岳)
summary: A volcano of 1,583 metres above Yufuin; about four and a half hours up and back from the central trailhead.

name: Chōjabaru Visitor Center (長者原ビジターセンター)
summary: At the northern trailhead for the Kujū mountains, beside Tadewara: trail and volcano information.

name: Aso Grassland Conservation Center (阿蘇草原保全活動センター)
summary: In Uchinomaki on the caldera floor: the grasslands, noyaki burning and how to volunteer.

name: Aso Volcano Museum (阿蘇火山博物館)
summary: Beside Kusasenri: the forces that shaped the Aso caldera and the Nakadake crater.

name: Karakunidake (韓国岳)
summary: The highest Kirishima summit, 1,700 metres, climbed from Ebino Kōgen; views over the crater lakes, Shinmoedake and, on clear days, Sakurajima. Check which trails are open.

name: Ōnamiike (大浪池)
summary: A round crater lake below Karakunidake, circled by a trail of about two hours; at its best in autumn colour.

name: Takachiho-no-mine (高千穂峰)
summary: The sacred mountain of the Kirishima range, a steep climb from Takachihogawara to the summit where myth says the gods descended.

name: Lake Miike (御池)
summary: A crater lake in forest on the Miyazaki side, with a lakeside campsite and good birdwatching.

name: Sakurajima and Yunohira Observatory (桜島・湯之平展望所)
summary: A viewpoint high on the flank of Kagoshima's restless volcano, looking up at the summit and across the bay. Sakurajima is 15 minutes by ferry from Kagoshima.

name: Kaimondake (開聞岳)
summary: A graceful volcanic cone at the southern tip of the Satsuma Peninsula.

name: Cape Sata (佐多岬)
summary: The southernmost point of mainland Japan: sea cliffs, subtropical palms and an observatory looking out over the ocean.

name: Ogawa Falls (雄川の滝)
summary: A waterfall in a gorge on the Ōsumi Peninsula, added to the park in 2018.

name: Takachihogawara Visitor Center (高千穂河原ビジターセンター)
summary: At the trailhead for Takachiho-no-mine: trail and volcano information.

name: Sakurajima Visitor Center (桜島ビジターセンター)
summary: Near the ferry terminal: Sakurajima's eruptions, how people live with them, and the lava-shore Nagisa promenade.

name: Jōmon Sugi (縄文杉)
summary: The best known of the ancient cedars, reached by a long day's hike from the Arakawa trailhead.

name: Shiratani Unsuikyō (白谷雲水峡)
summary: A ravine of moss-covered rocks, streams and old cedars, with trails of several lengths; the longest climbs to the viewpoint of Taikoiwa rock.

name: Miyanouradake (宮之浦岳)
summary: Kyushu's highest summit, 1,936 metres, above dwarf bamboo and weathered granite outcrops; a long day's climb.

name: Yakusugi Land (ヤクスギランド)
summary: Forest trails of different lengths among yakusugi cedars and moss, in the mountains above Anbō.

name: Ōko-no-taki (大川の滝)
summary: An 88-metre waterfall near the south-west coast, one of Japan's Top 100 Waterfalls.

name: Nagata-hama (永田浜)
summary: Beaches on the north-west coast where loggerhead turtles nest from May to July; night viewing only on organised watches.

name: Kuchinoerabujima (口永良部島)
summary: An active volcanic island west of Yakushima, with simple hot springs, sea cliffs, tide pools and the rare Erabu flying fox.

name: Yakushima World Heritage Conservation Center (屋久島世界遺産センター)
summary: The Ministry of the Environment's centre at Anbō: trail conditions, the World Heritage forest and the mountain rules.

name: Yakusugi Museum (屋久杉自然館)
summary: The cedars, the logging era and the forest; the Arakawa shuttle bus leaves from here.

name: Kinsakubaru (金作原)
summary: Old subtropical forest with giant evergreen oaks on Amami Ōshima, visited with a certified local guide along a forest road.

name: Sumiyō Mangroves (住用のマングローブ林)
summary: One of Japan's largest mangrove forests, at the mouths of the Sumiyō and Yakugachi rivers; explore it by kayak.

name: Yuwandake (湯湾岳)
summary: Amami Ōshima's highest mountain, cloaked in evergreen forest and often in cloud.

name: Ayamaru Cape (あやまる岬)
summary: A headland on the Kasari Peninsula looking over coral reefs and the open sea.

name: Inokawadake (井之川岳)
summary: A forested mountain on Tokunoshima, known for its ferns and endemic plants.

name: Mushiro-se (ムシロ瀬)
summary: Broad rock shelves cut flat by the waves on Tokunoshima's north coast.

name: Shōryūdō Cave (昇竜洞)
summary: A limestone cave on Okinoerabujima, one of hundreds on the island, with a lit section open to visitors.

name: Yurigahama (百合ヶ浜)
summary: A white sandbar that appears off Yoron at low tide, changing shape and position from year to year.

name: Amami Wildlife Center (奄美野生生物保護センター)
summary: The Ministry of the Environment's conservation centre in Yamato village: the islands' wildlife, the mongoose campaign and forest rules.

name: Cape Hedo (辺戸岬)
summary: The northern tip of Okinawa Island: limestone sea cliffs, views over the open sea and a monument to the end of the US occupation.

name: Daisekirinzan (大石林山)
summary: Limestone karst near Cape Hedo, weathered into pinnacles and stone forest.

name: Hiji Falls (比地大滝)
summary: At 25.7 metres the tallest waterfall on Okinawa Island, at the end of a 1.5-kilometre forest trail beside the Hiji River.

name: Yonahadake (与那覇岳)
summary: A forested summit at the heart of Yambaru's mountains.

name: Gesashi Bay Mangroves (慶佐次湾のヒルギ林)
summary: The largest mangrove forest on Okinawa Island, with a boardwalk and canoe tours up the river.

name: Okinawa Rail Ecology Center (ヤンバルクイナ生態展示学習施設)
summary: Kunigami village's centre for the Okinawa rail and its protection.

name: Yambaru Wildlife Conservation Center Ufugi Nature Museum (やんばる野生生物保護センター ウフギー自然館)
summary: The Ministry of the Environment's centre in Kunigami: Yambaru's wildlife, conservation and current rules.

name: Furuzamami Beach (古座間味ビーチ)
summary: A long white beach on Zamami with reefs and fish a few strokes offshore; one of the best snorkelling beaches in the islands.

name: Aharen Beach (阿波連ビーチ)
summary: Tokashiki's main beach, on the west coast beside Aharen village: fine sand, snorkelling and sunsets.

name: Inazaki Observatory (稲崎展望台)
summary: A lookout on the north-west of Zamami, among the best places to watch for humpback whales in winter.

name: Western Observatory, Tokashiki (西展望台)
summary: A lookout on the west side of Tokashiki, with views over the sea to the other Kerama islands.

name: Nishibama, Aka (阿嘉島 北浜)
summary: A white beach on Aka with coral and turtles offshore; bridges link Aka to Geruma and Fukaji.

name: Geruma (慶留間島)
summary: A small island linked to Aka by bridge, with the Takara residence, an Important Cultural Property, and Kerama deer.

name: Urauchi River and Mariyudu Falls (浦内川・マリユドゥの滝)
summary: Take a boat up Okinawa's longest river through mangrove and jungle, then walk to the broad, stepped falls of Mariyudu and on to Kanpire.

name: Pinaisara Falls (ピナイサーラの滝)
summary: At 55 metres the tallest waterfall in Okinawa Prefecture, reached by kayak and trail up the Hinai River — a capped, permit-only route.

name: Nakama River (仲間川)
summary: Sightseeing boats run up through Japan's largest mangrove forest to a giant sakishima-suō tree.

name: Hoshizuna-no-hama (星砂の浜)
summary: A beach on Iriomote's north coast whose 'star sand' is the shells of tiny marine organisms.

name: Kabira Bay (川平湾)
summary: A bay of white sand, islets and luminous water on Ishigaki's north coast; see the coral from a glass-bottomed boat.

name: Cape Hirakubo (平久保崎)
summary: Ishigaki's northern tip, with a lighthouse and views over reefs and open sea.

name: Shiraho (白保)
summary: A reef on Ishigaki's east coast famous for its huge blue coral colony; snorkel or take a glass-bottomed boat.

name: Nagura Amparu (名蔵アンパル)
summary: Mangroves and tidal flats on Ishigaki's west coast, a Ramsar site and a stopping place for migrating birds.

name: Iriomote Wildlife Conservation Center (西表野生生物保護センター)
summary: The Ministry of the Environment's centre at Komi on Iriomote: the Iriomote cat, its protection and the island's wildlife.

name: Taketomi Island Visitor Center Yugafukan (竹富島ビジターセンター ゆがふ館)
summary: Taketomi's island culture, village and reefs.

name: Anárjohka
summary: The border river with Finland, Inarijoki in Finnish. It rises in the park and flows north to join the Kárášjohka and form the Tana.

name: Gavdnjajávri
summary: The largest lake in the park, on the open vidda west of the Anárjohka.

name: Kárášjohka
summary: The headwaters of the river that gives Karasjok its name, rising in the western part of the park.

name: Bávttajohka
summary: One of the larger rivers draining the park northward towards the Tana.

name: Goššjohka
summary: The valley used as a northern way in: a road of about 12 kilometres up the valley, then about 15 kilometres on foot to the park boundary.

name: Skiehččanjohka
summary: One of the park's larger rivers, in the eastern part of the park near the Finnish border.

name: Midtiklumpen
summary: Åakerebahke in South Sámi. The park's highest summit, 1,333 metres, in the Blåfjella massif of the north-east.

name: Skjækerhatten
summary: Huvhpie in South Sámi. The landmark peak of the southern Skjækerfjella, where the park's valleys are greenest.

name: Skjækerdalen
summary: The southern valley named in the park's protection purpose as one of its most important landscapes; trails lead in from Vera and Skjækerfossen.

name: Gaundalen
summary: A valley named in the park's protection purpose, with a mountain farm that visitors reach by boat from the Swedish side.

name: Holderen
summary: A lake with Holden mountain farm on its shore, now a waypoint on the route between Gaundalen and Gjevsjøen.

name: Gjevsjøen
summary: The lake beside Gjefsjøen farm, base of the American Operation Rype in the spring of 1945.

name: Bukvassfjellet
summary: Bare gneiss fells in the barren north, once Gressåmoen National Park, where moose and deer may still not be hunted.

name: Lierne Nasjonalparksenter
summary: The authorised visitor centre for Blåfjella-Skjækerfjella and Lierne, at Nordli, with an exhibition on living from nature and with predators, and a geology park outside.

name: Holden fjellgård (Bekkstugu)
summary: DNT cabin

name: Skjækerdalshytta
summary: DNT cabin

name: Nørdre Hestbreapiggen
summary: The park's highest summit, 2,172 metres, in the Hestbreapiggan massif between Bøverdalen and Lundadalen.

name: Tverrådalskyrkja
summary: Perhaps Breheimen's best-known peak, 2,088 metres, towering beside the route from Sota to Nørdstedalseter.

name: Lundadalsvatnet
summary: A long mountain lake at about 1,150 metres beneath Hestbreapiggan, in the upper Lundadalen of Skjåk.

name: Lendbreen
summary: A shrinking ice patch on an ancient mountain pass, used from about AD 300 to 1500; melting ice has revealed a 1,700-year-old tunic.

name: Harbardsbreen
summary: One of the park's larger glaciers, in the high country of Luster between Jostedalen and Fortunsdalen.

name: Spørteggbreen
summary: One of the larger glaciers on the Norwegian mainland, in the south-west of the park between Jostedalsbreen and Harbardsbreen.

name: Holåbreen
summary: A glacier on the boundary between Skjåk and Luster, under the Holåtindan peaks.

name: Norsk Fjellsenter
summary: The Norwegian Mountain Centre in Lom, authorised visitor centre for Breheimen, Jotunheimen and Reinheimen, with the exhibition 'Bergtatt'.

name: Breheimsenteret
summary: Authorised visitor centre for Breheimen and Jostedalsbreen in Jostedalen, with exhibitions on glaciers and climate, and a base for glacier walks.

name: Fortunsdalen besøkssenter
summary: Authorised visitor centre for Breheimen and Jotunheimen in Fortun, at the foot of the Sognefjellet road, with a café.

name: Arentzbu
summary: DNT cabin

name: Slæom
summary: DNT cabin

name: Sprongdalshytta
summary: DNT cabin

name: Trulsbu
summary: DNT cabin

name: Kvigtinden
summary: Voenjelensnjurhtjie in South Sámi. The park's highest peak, 1,699 metres, in the dark granite chain of the west.

name: Simskardet
summary: Sijdurrie. A pass in the north-west and a much-used way into the western part; the Simskard round is the park authority's suggestion for a day walk.

name: Simskardvatnet
summary: One of the two largest lakes in the park's central basin, between the western peaks and the eastern fells.

name: Orvatnet
summary: Ovrejaevrie, also written Orrevatnet. The other great lake of the central basin, in the south of the park.

name: Jetnamsklumpen
summary: Jitnemensnuhkie. A rounded summit of the eastern fells, close to the Swedish border.

name: Rainesfjellet
summary: Raajnese. Fells of bare, vegetation-free boulder field in the east — Børgefjell at its starkest.

name: Storhøe
summary: The park's highest point, 1,716 metres, in its western half.

name: Falketind
summary: A 1,684-metre summit in the high centre of the park.

name: Halvfarhøe
summary: One of the park's highest summits, at nearly 1,690 metres.

name: Kattuglehøe
summary: Fells in the south-east of the park, protected within it as the Kattuglehøi nature reserve.

name: Besøkssenter villrein
summary: The authorised wild reindeer visitor centre at Hjerkinn, with an exhibition in Fjellportalen; Viewpoint Snøhetta lies 1.5 kilometres to the north-west.

name: Snøhetta
summary: The park's natural centre, 2,286 metres, and its great draw. The usual ascent starts at Snøheim, reached by shuttle bus from Hjerkinn.

name: Storstyggesvånåtinden
summary: Also called Storsvånåtinden: a peak of over 2,200 metres in the Svånåtindan range, about 5 km south-west of Snøhetta.

name: Storskrymten
summary: 1,985 metres, the highest mountain in Trøndelag, where Oppdal, Sunndal and Lesja meet.

name: Stroplsjødalen
summary: A heath-covered valley in the eastern part of the park and sensitive wild reindeer country; the park board's marked Muskox Trail keeps walkers out of it.

name: Besøkssenter villrein
summary: The authorised wild reindeer visitor centre at Hjerkinn, with the park's information and offices; a short walk leads to Viewpoint Snøhetta, looking into the park.

name: Loennechenbua
summary: DNT cabin

name: Raubergshytta
summary: DNT cabin

name: Reinheim
summary: DNT cabin

name: Åmotdalshytta
summary: DNT cabin

name: Storviglen
summary: The park's highest fell, 1,561 metres, at its northern edge.

name: Røa
summary: The river through the heart of the park's lake country, in a landscape where water covers more than a tenth of the ground.

name: Stor-Svuku
summary: Svahke in South Sámi. A fell of 1,421 metres in the south of the park, climbed from the DNT cabin Svukuriset.

name: Elgåhogna
summary: At 1,460 metres the highest of the southern fells, near Elgå.

name: Grøthogna
summary: A 1,401-metre fell near the Swedish border, rising above the river Røa.

name: Besøkssenter nasjonalpark Femundsmarka og Gutulia
summary: The authorised visitor centre at Elgå, the southern stop of the lake boat, in a building inspired by Sámi tradition. Open through the summer, with shorter hours the rest of the year.

name: Muggsjølia
summary: Run by Statskog

name: Møllerbua
summary: Run by Statskog

name: Røvollen
summary: DNT cabin

name: Folgefonni
summary: The ice cap itself, in three parts — Nordre, Midtre and Søndre Folgefonna. At its highest the ice reached 1,662 metres in 2013.

name: Bondhusbreen
summary: A crevassed glacier arm flowing down towards Bondhusdalen and the Maurangsfjord on the western side.

name: Buarbreen
summary: A glacier arm reaching down into Buardalen, about 6 km south-west of Odda, split in two by a small peak.

name: Melderskin
summary: A 1,426-metre peak above Rosendal, inside the park — the nearest mountain higher than Ben Nevis.

name: Skjeggesnuten
summary: A lime-rich mountain in the south of the park; with Sauanuten, it carries the park's richest mountain flora.

name: Sauanuten
summary: A summit on lime-rich rock in the south-east, part of the same rich mountain flora.

name: Folgefonnsenteret
summary: The authorised visitor centre for Folgefonna National Park in Rosendal, with an interactive exhibition from 2017; the Stone Park, on the peninsula's geology, is ten minutes' walk away.

summary: DNT cabin

name: Holmaskjer
summary: DNT cabin

summary: DNT cabin

name: Forlandsletta
summary: The 19-km-long low coastal plain that nearly divides the island, in its southern half.

name: Forlandsøyane
summary: Three small islands off the west coast of Forlandsletta: a bird reserve and Ramsar site, closed to all traffic from 15 May to 15 August.

name: Poolepynten
summary: A 1.5-km-long point on Forlandsundet, named after the whaler Jonas Poole.

name: Monacofjellet
summary: At 1,084 metres the northernmost mountain of the Grampianfjella chain in the north of the island.

name: Richardlaguna
summary: A lagoon about 7 km long on the island's eastern coast.

name: Fuglehuken
summary: The northern point of the island — the English whalers' Fair Foreland — with cultural remains on its coast.

name: Plankeholmane
summary: About twenty skerries and islets off the island's southern tip: a bird reserve closed to all traffic from 15 May to 15 August.

name: Forollhogna
summary: The park's highest summit, 1,332 metres, where Os, Holtålen and Midtre Gauldal meet; the pilgrim road passes at its foot.

name: Forollsjøen
summary: The lake at the centre of the park, below Forollhogna's summit.

name: Gjersjøhøa
summary: Fells in Tolga, in the far south-west of the park, within the range of its wild reindeer herd.

name: Litj-Hiåsjøhytta
summary: Run by Kvikne Fjellstyre

name: Slottet
summary: 'The Castle', 1,047 metres — the highest point of both the Norwegian and the Swedish park.

name: Brynflået
summary: The border on the southern plateau, reached by a well-marked path from Storbekkåsen whose steepest section is stone-paved.

name: Bråtafallet
summary: A waterfall in Bergådalen, at the park's western edge, with a rest area beside it.

name: Gira
summary: One of the two rivers that cut the Norwegian plateau into three.

name: Storgnollen
summary: With Steinknøsen and Furuknøsen, a stretch of boulder fields, gorges and steep relief prized for its landscape and its traces of the ice age.

name: Naturum Fulufjället
summary: In Sweden: the visitor centre of Fulufjällets nationalpark, at its main entrance by the Njupeskär waterfall, and a good starting point for walks and for learning about both parks.

name: Færder fyr
summary: A 43-metre cast-iron lighthouse on Tristein (Lille Færder), first lit in 1857 and protected since 1997, marking the entrance to the outer Oslofjord.

name: Store Færder
summary: The island where the first Færder light was lit in 1697, with the remains of the old lighthouse and its protected buildings.

name: Østre Bolæren
summary: The main island destination, with coastal paths, a defence museum, a café and a summer boat service; 907 species of butterfly and moth have been recorded here.

name: Grevestuen
summary: On Mellom Bolæren, one of the oldest hunting lodges in Norway.

name: Sandø
summary: An island rich in plants and insects, with ice-polished rock; tents are not allowed here.

name: Lille Rauer
summary: A small island in the bird-protection zone and the refuge of the threatened yellow horned poppy.

name: Besøkssenter Færder nasjonalpark
summary: The authorised visitor centre at Verdens ende, 'World's End', just outside the boundary — exhibitions, guided walks and a fine view over the islands, with Moutmarka's walking country next door.

name: Gutulisetra
summary: Three summer farms worked from 1750 to 1949, with 16 restored timber buildings and a 1.5 km nature trail; in summer, hosts serve coffee and waffles at Nedpåvollen.

name: Oppåvollen
summary: The uppermost of the three farms, with a small exhibition on two hundred years of summer-farm life.

name: Gutulivola
summary: The park's central fell, 949 metres, its slopes clothed in open old pine forest.

name: Valsjøen
summary: A good fishing lake in the mires east of Gutulivola, draining east towards Sweden.

name: Gutulisjøen
summary: The lake on the park's western edge; the path in follows its shore from the car park.

name: Besøkssenter nasjonalpark Femundsmarka og Gutulia
summary: The authorised visitor centre at Elgå, a short drive north, which also hosts visitors at Gutulisetra in summer.

name: Folarskardnuten
summary: The highest point of Hallingskarvet, 1,933 metres, on the summit plateau above the north and south scarps.

name: Prestholtskarvet
summary: The eastern end of the massif. A 6.5 km path from Prestholtseter, partly paved in stone by Sherpas from Nepal, climbs to a viewpoint at 1,705 metres.

name: Folarskardet
summary: A pass through the massif, where Lordehytta, the dry-stone hut of the reindeer-hunting Lord Garvagh, has stood since 1880.

name: Flakavatnet
summary: A high, cold lake at 1,453 metres in a hollow of the massif's western end.

name: Vargebreen
summary: Also written Vargabreen: the glacier in the high mountains at the park's western end.

name: Raggsteindalen
summary: A valley on the north side of the massif, partly inside the park.

name: Hårteigen
summary: A 1,690-metre block of rock rising from the western vidda, visible from much of the plateau — Hardangervidda's landmark.

name: Litlosvatnet
summary: A lake on the western vidda by the Litlos lodge, in the dramatic country near Hårteigen.

name: Nordmannslågen
summary: A great lake in the heart of the plateau, on the Eidfjord side, in classic trout-fishing country.

name: Bjornesfjorden
summary: A long lake on the open, gentler eastern vidda in Nore og Uvdal.

name: Langesjøen
summary: A lake on the eastern vidda in Nore og Uvdal, among wide moorland and mires.

name: Norsk Natursenter
summary: The authorised visitor centre in Øvre Eidfjord, near Vøringsfossen, with a panoramic film and exhibitions on landscape, wildlife and climate. Open late March to October; check before you go.

name: Hardangervidda nasjonalparksenter
summary: The authorised visitor centre at Skinnarbu, south of the vidda by Møsvatn, with an award-winning interactive wild reindeer exhibition, a nature trail and a café with a wide view.

name: Austfjorden

name: Vestfjorden

name: Kapp Petermann
summary: The northern point of the peninsula that splits the fjord into Austfjorden and Vestfjorden.

name: Austfjordnes
summary: A point on the east side of Austfjorden with a trapping station still used today.

name: Krosspynten
summary: A point at the mouth of Vestfjorden, where a trapper's cabin was built in 1910.

name: Purpurdalen
summary: A valley on the west side of the fjord in Andrée Land, with a trapper's cabin from 1912.

summary: A small lake in Ny-Friesland on the east shore, with Arctic char.

name: Jomfruland
summary: The island itself: a moraine ridge with a pebble beach almost seven kilometres long on the Skagerrak side and sandy coves, meadows and woods on the landward side.

name: Jomfruland fyr
summary: Two white lighthouses side by side mid-island, a brick tower first lit in 1839 and its cast-iron successor. The old tower can be climbed in summer.

name: Tårntjernet
summary: The island's largest pond, just by the lighthouses. Theodor Kittelsen took inspiration here for his painting «Nøkken», the water spirit of Norwegian folklore.

name: Øitangen
summary: The northern tip of Jomfruland, where the coastal migration of birds passes in spring and autumn and the Jomfruland bird station rings and counts them.

name: Stråholmen
summary: A small moraine island two kilometres north of Jomfruland, with no ferry, sheep grazing all year and a seabird reserve in the south, closed 15 April to 15 July.

name: Stangnes
summary: The park's one corner on the mainland, at its south-western end and reached by road: smooth ice-scoured rock, shallow sand and kelp just offshore.

name: Besøkssenter Jomfruland nasjonalpark
summary: The park's authorised visitor centre, in the old lighthouse keeper's house beside the towers, with an interactive exhibition on nature above and below the water. Open daily in high summer.

name: Nigardsbreen
summary: The arm that had crushed the farm Nigard by 1748, now with the lake Nigardsbrevatnet in front of it in Jostedalen. Guided glacier walks start nearby.

name: Briksdalsbreen
summary: A steep arm at the head of Oldedalen, about 25 kilometres south of Olden, now ending on dry land behind the small lake it once covered.

name: Bøyabreen
summary: An arm in Fjærland that reaches far down its valley, to about 300 metres above sea level.

name: Kjenndalsbreen
summary: A glacier arm at the head of Kjenndalen, above Loen on the Nordfjord side.

name: Lodalskåpa
summary: At 2,083 metres the highest peak in the park, for a long time a nunatak ringed by the ice.

name: Høgste Breakulen
summary: The highest point of the ice plateau itself, a broad white dome in the middle of the glacier.

name: Jostedalsbreen Nasjonalparksenter
summary: Authorised visitor centre by Oppstrynsvatnet on the north side, with a botanical garden, a geological park, a film and an exhibition.

name: Norsk Bremuseum
summary: The Norwegian Glacier Museum in Fjærland, an authorised visitor centre on glaciers and climate, in a building by Sverre Fehn.

name: Breheimsenteret
summary: Authorised visitor centre in Jostedalen for Jostedalsbreen and Breheimen, the starting point for glacier walks, kayaking and rafting.
