summary: The narrow ridge between green Gjende and blue Bessvatnet. The classic day takes the boat to Memurubu and walks back over the ridge to Gjendesheim.

name: Gjende
summary: An 18-kilometre glacial lake coloured green by rock flour. Boats run between Gjendesheim, Memurubu and Gjendebu from early June to late September; check the timetable before you go.

name: Glittertind
summary: Norway's second-highest mountain, 2,452 metres. The summit ice cap that once rivalled Galdhøpiggen's height has all but melted away. Reached from Spiterstulen or from Glitterheim.

name: Store Skagastølstind
summary: Storen, 2,405 metres, the highest peak of the jagged Hurrungane. A rock climb, first made by William Cecil Slingsby in 1876.

name: Knutshøe
summary: The ridge across Gjende from Besseggen, and the other candidate for Peer Gynt's reindeer ride in Ibsen's play.

name: Smørstabbtindane
summary: Glacier-hung peaks above the Sognefjellet road, a favourite for ski touring in spring.

name: Norsk Fjellsenter
summary: The authorised visitor centre for Jotunheimen, Breheimen and Reinheimen, in Lom, with the exhibition «Bergtatt» and route advice.

name: Utladalen Naturhus
summary: Authorised visitor centre for Jotunheimen in Utladalen, on the way to Vettisfossen.

name: Fannaråkhytta
summary: DNT cabin

name: Gjendebu
summary: DNT cabin

name: Gjertvasshytta
summary: Run by Luster Austre fjellstyre

name: Glitterheim
summary: DNT cabin

name: Memurubu
summary: DNT cabin

name: Olavsbu
summary: DNT cabin

name: Balvatnet
summary: Bállávrre in Lule Sámi: the large lake of the northern upland, south of Sulitjelma. A hydropower reservoir, it is left out of the park, which surrounds it.

name: Junkerdalsura
summary: A separate nature reserve beside the park's south-western edge: a forested slope from valley floor to bare mountain, famous among botanists for its plants.

name: Solvågtinden
summary: The prominent peak above Junkerdalen at the park's southern edge, with views down the valley.

name: Jakobsbakken
summary: A mountain mining village of Sulitjelma, home to up to 400 people around 1920; the mine closed in 1968. Now a gateway to the park.

name: Fuglvatnet
summary: A lake in the northern upland, just north-west of Balvatnet.

name: Bjørntoppen
summary: A summit in the south of the park, above the valley of Rykkjedalen.

name: Besøkssenter nasjonalpark Nordland
summary: The authorised visitor centre at Storjord in Saltdal, with exhibitions on geology, wildlife and Sámi and traditional use, beside the Adde Zetterquist art gallery.

name: Argaladhytta
summary: DNT cabin

name: Balvasshytta
summary: DNT cabin

name: Tjalalveshytta
summary: DNT cabin

name: Skaget
summary: One of the park's two landmark summits, 1,685 metres, in the west above Øystre Slidre. The national park path leads towards it from the car park at Storeskag.

name: Langsua
summary: The fell that gives the park its name, 1,553 metres high, with wide views over the low mountains around it.

name: Ormtjernkampen
summary: A 1,128-metre hill above old spruce forest in the south-east, protected as Norway's smallest national park from 1968 until Langsua absorbed it.

name: Dokkfaret
summary: A valley of massive old pines, some 300 to 400 years old, along the summer road from Holsbru to Liomseter, protected as a landscape area beside the park.

name: Holsfossen
summary: The waterfall at Holsbru, a south-eastern entrance to the park, with parking, information and a trekking-association café.

name: Hersjømyrin
summary: A wetland nature reserve of mires beside the park's northern edge, protected at the same time as the park. The information point at Veslefjell looks out over it.

name: Kittilbu utmarksmuseum
summary: An outfield museum in Gausdal Vestfjell with exhibitions, information on the park, a café, nature and cultural trails and a bird hide nearby. Not an authorised national park centre.

name: Fossbekkbua
summary: Run by Gausdal Fjellstyre

name: Langsubua
summary: Run by Gausdal Fjellstyre

name: Reinsjøbua
summary: Run by Gausdal Fjellstyre

name: Skriurusten
summary: DNT cabin

name: Skytterbua
summary: Run by Gausdal Fjellstyre

name: Storkvelvbu
summary: DNT cabin

name: Hestkjøltoppen
summary: The highest summit in the park, 1,390 metres, on the Hestkjølen massif. There is no marked route: go only in clear weather, with map and compass.

name: Hestkjølen
summary: The upland massif that fills the centre of the park, also called Hartkjølen, with bare tops above tarns and mires.

name: Fiskløysdalen
summary: A valley in the east of the park. For fit, experienced walkers, the park suggests a summer round trip up Lutterdalen and back down Fiskløysdalen.

name: Muru
summary: The valley north of the park, outside its boundary, with the main entrance at Øvre jakthytta; a marked, partly boardwalked trail leads about three kilometres to the memorial stone inside.

name: Raudbergtjønna
summary: A tarn about a kilometre north of the park boundary, where Nordli fjellstyre rents out Raudberghytta, at an entry point for Hestkjølen and the park.

name: Lierne Nasjonalparksenter
summary: The authorised visitor centre for Lierne and Blåfjella-Skjækerfjella in Nordli, with the exhibition «Å leve av naturen – å leve med rovdyr» and an outdoor geology park.

name: Bunes
summary: A broad white beach on the outer coast below steep peaks, reached on foot over the low pass Einangen from Vindstad, which most visitors reach by passenger boat from Reine.

name: Kvalvika
summary: A beach in a cove on the open Atlantic side of Moskenesøya, just outside the park, reached on foot from Fredvang or Innersand. No cycling on the path from Torsfjorden.

name: Ryten
summary: The 543-metre summit above Kvalvika on Moskenesøya, a gentle walk that ends abruptly above the open sea.

name: Hermannsdalstinden
summary: At 1,029 metres the highest peak on Moskenesøya, about 6.5 kilometres west of Reine.

name: Helvetestinden
summary: The polished 602-metre peak rising above the beach at Bunes.

name: Ågvatnet
summary: A lake above Å at the southern end of the island, just outside the park, with the sandy Melkarsanden on its shore.

name: Kollhellaren, Refsvika
summary: A cave 115 metres long with about 30 figures painted some 3,000 years ago. Visits only with an authorised guide.

name: Besøkssenter Lofotodden nasjonalpark
summary: The park's authorised visitor centre in the middle of Reine, with exhibitions, films and tourist information; open all year, but check hours and prices before you go.

name: Searvoesvuemie (Sørvassdalen)
summary: The valley where Gippe and Gunnar Njarka built their turf hut in 1917, now protected, restored and open to walkers for the night.

name: Skjørlægda
summary: An old mountain farm reached from the east, a good day walk for families; once its own nature reserve.

name: Krongelvatnet
summary: A lake in the west of the park, known for its fishing.

name: Visten
summary: The fjord on the park's western side, reached by express boat, with farms beneath steep walls and a strong tidal current.

name: Vistkjerringa
summary: One of the high summits of Vistfjellan, the massif at the heart of the park.

name: Eiterådalen
summary: A valley along the park's eastern side.

name: Blåfjellet
summary: The mountain in the far south-east of the park, in Grane, above Svenningdalen.

name: Corbels canyon
summary: A cleft in the karst where the cave system beneath the mountain shows at the surface.

name: Láhko
summary: A karst basin in the high limestone country at the heart of the park, bearing the park's Lule Sámi name.

name: Svalvatnet
summary: A lake in the south-west of the park, among low alpine heaths and late snowbeds.

name: Store Sandvatnet
summary: A lake on the park's western side, near Svalvatnet.

name: Nordre Glomvassfjellet
summary: The summit where Láhko meets Saltfjellet-Svartisen National Park at a single point.

name: Besøkssenter nasjonalpark Nordland
summary: The authorised visitor centre at Storjord in Saltdal, with exhibitions on geology, wildlife and Sámi and traditional use.

name: Kvitsteindalsgammen
summary: DNT cabin

name: Møysalen
summary: At 1,262 metres the highest mountain in Vesterålen and Lofoten. Every route to the top crosses a steep summit glacier; the view on a clear day rivals any in Norway.

name: Vestpollen
summary: The sheltered fjord arm at the head of Øksfjorden that brings the park down to the sea; the start of the south-eastern route up Vestpolldalen to the summit.

name: Vestpolldalen
summary: The valley running up from Vestpollen, with seashore meadows at the river mouth and green birch slopes.

name: Vestpolltinden
summary: A peak above Vestpollen; on its south-western side the galleries of an old mine can still be seen.

name: Nordtinden
summary: One of the summits in the eastern part of the park.

name: Snytindan
summary: The cluster of peaks on the park's north-eastern edge, at the meeting of Lødingen, Sortland and Kvæfjord.

name: Alkhornet
summary: The cliff at the northern mouth of Isfjorden, a seabird colony above a green slope where Arctic foxes den. Keep well away from the dens.

name: Trygghamna
summary: The 'safe harbour': a sheltered bay with whalers' tryworks, Russian Pomor ruins and graves, and two glaciers at its head. Do not walk on the ruins.

name: Daudmannsøyra
summary: A coastal plain some 23 kilometres long, wetland and tundra important for geese and waders.

name: Bohemanneset
summary: The spit at the tip of Bohemanflya, a peninsula claimed for its coal in 1899. The islets to the south are a bird reserve, closed 15 May to 15 August.

name: Ekmanfjorden
summary: An 18-kilometre arm of Nordfjorden where the glacier Sefströmbreen reaches the sea beside the island of Coraholmen.

name: Kapp Wijk
summary: A broad point in Dickson Land with a trappers' station, three generations of huts and still in use.

name: Skansbukta
summary: A sheltered bay under the cliffs of Skansen, with the remains of a gypsum mine and warmth-loving plants on the slope. Keep off the scree.

name: Gravneset, Magdalenefjorden
summary: A whalers' cemetery of about 130 graves from the 1600s to the late 1700s and four blubber ovens, below glaciers. Keep outside the fences.

name: Smeerenburg
summary: The main Dutch whaling station of the early 1600s, on Amsterdamøya. Rings of 'blubber cement' mark the ovens; do not step on them.

name: Virgohamna
summary: The bay on Danskøya where Andrée launched his polar balloon in 1897 and Wellman based his airships. Protected remains; check the Governor's access rules.

name: Ytre Norskøya
summary: Nine Dutch blubber ovens along a beach and one of Svalbard's largest burial grounds, 165 graves. Parts of the site are closed all year.

name: Jotunkjeldene, Bockfjorden
summary: Warm springs near the shore, at 20 °C or more all year, building fragile carbonate terraces. Walk on the moraine, never on the deposits.

name: Monacobreen
summary: One of the park's two great glaciers, calving into the head of Liefdefjorden. Keep well back from the ice front.

name: Reinsdyrflya
summary: The largest strandflat in Svalbard: a low plain of old beaches and tundra between the open sea and Woodfjorden.

name: Moffen
summary: A low gravel island just north of 80° North and a walrus haul-out. All traffic, by sea or air below 500 metres, is banned from 15 May to 15 September.

name: Lloyds hotel
summary: Run by Governor of Svalbard

name: Spornes
summary: The start of the long boulder beach on Tromøy's outer shore, where the moraine runs on from Spornes to Hoveodden, fringed by wind-bent woods.

name: Hoveodden
summary: The south-western point of Tromøy, with sandy, shallow beaches on its sheltered side and fire pans for visitors. A national park portal stands near Hove.

name: Merdø
summary: A car-free island and old outport with sandy beaches and the Merdøgaard museum. Ferries run every half hour in summer.

name: Store Torungen fyr
summary: The cast-iron lighthouse of 1914 on an outer island, reached only by boat. Lille Torungen nearby is the survivor of the twin towers first lit in 1844.

name: Lyngør fyr
summary: A lighthouse of 1879 on Kjeholmen at the park's north-eastern end, reached only by boat. The site is open to the public.

name: Hasseltangen
summary: Where Raet comes ashore in Grimstad: a sheltered, child-friendly beach on the inside, rough rocky coast on the outside and views to the Torungen lighthouses.

name: Molen
summary: The top of the moraine breaking the surface east of Tromøy as an islet of loose pebbles about 130 metres long, in waters known as a ships' graveyard.

name: Besøkssenter nasjonalpark Raet
summary: The authorised visitor centre, inside Vitensenteret Sørlandet in Arendal, with an exhibition on the park's seabirds and a saltwater aquarium of kelp-forest fish.

name: Litlverivassforsen
summary: The lake Litlverivatnet pours straight over the mountainside into Storskogdalen in a fall of 223 metres. A day walk from the road.

name: Storskogdalen
summary: The main valley, with its river falling in rapids and waterfalls between old pine forest and steep crags.

name: Storskogvatnet
summary: A lake ringed by old pine forest, where 20 red-listed fungi grow on dead and fallen trees.

name: Litlverivatnet
summary: The lake above Litlverivassforsen, set in bare, ice-smoothed granite.

name: Storskogtinden
summary: The summit rising directly above Storskogvatnet.

name: Lappfjellet
summary: The high ground in the south of the park, with small glaciers and snow that lies all year.

name: Lakshol
summary: The farm west of the park, at the end of the road from the E6, where the path up Storskogdalen to Storskogvatnet begins.

name: Besøkssenter nasjonalpark Nordland
summary: The authorised visitor centre at Storjord in Saltdal, with exhibitions on geology, wildlife and Sámi and traditional use.

name: Trollveggen (the Troll Wall)
summary: Often called Europe's tallest vertical rock face, on the Trolltindane above Romsdalen; first climbed in 1965. Seen best from the valley road and railway.

name: Trollstigen
summary: The hairpin mountain road at the park's north-western edge, and a gateway to the Trolltindane and the high ground beyond.

name: Puttegga
summary: One of the summits of Tafjordfjella, the steep western massif crossed by marked routes between tourist huts.

name: Zakariasdammen
summary: A dam above Tafjord, and the western gateway into Tafjordfjella.

name: Digervarden
summary: A 1,780-metre mountain in Lesja whose melting ice patch gave up a pair of 1,300-year-old skis in 2014 and 2021.

name: Gråhøe
summary: The massif at the heart of the park, between Grotli and Lesjaskog, in the wild reindeer's high country.

name: Billingen
summary: A summer-farm settlement in Skjåk on the park's southern edge, one of its marked gateways.

name: Norsk Fjellsenter
summary: Authorised visitor centre in Lom for Reinheimen, Jotunheimen and Breheimen, with a separate exhibition on Reinheimen and its wild reindeer.

name: Norsk Tindesenter
summary: Authorised visitor centre in Åndalsnes, on the history of Norwegian mountaineering and on Reinheimen.

name: Pyttbua
summary: DNT cabin

name: Tjønnebu
summary: DNT cabin

name: Torsbu
summary: DNT cabin

name: Vakkerstøylen
summary: DNT cabin

name: Mollisfossen
summary: The greatest of the valley's falls: 269 metres in three steps from the plateau into Reisadalen.

name: Imofossen
summary: A waterfall at Imo, upstream of Nedrefoss, where two rivers meet in a narrow gorge scoured with potholes.

name: Sarafossen
summary: A fine waterfall near the gateway at Ovi Raishiin, a day walk from there; it lies some 8 km outside the park itself.

name: Sieimma
summary: A historic stopping place on the river path, one of the day-walk goals from Ovi Raishiin.

name: Ráisjávri
summary: A lake in the east of the park, with an unlocked hut; from here the Nordkalottruta and the historic walking route follow the Reisa down to Sieimma.

name: Ovi Raishiin
summary: Kven for 'the door into Reisadalen': the park's gateway, about 8 km outside it, with parking, maps, a nature trail, a mountain library, a viewpoint and a cabin to rent.

name: Besøkssenter Reisa nasjonalpark
summary: The authorised visitor centre at Halti nasjonalparksenter in Storslett, with information and an exhibition on the park.

name: Immogammen
summary: Run by Statskog

name: Nedrefosshytta
summary: DNT cabin

name: Sørdalen gorge (Boldnoávži)
summary: A deep canyon cut by Ice Age meltwater between glaciated peaks. The Arctic Trail follows Sørdalen to Lappjord, with views down into the gorge.

name: Rohkunborri
summary: The massif that gives the park its name, rising above the wooded valleys and wetlands of the east.

name: Geavdnjajávri
summary: A large, deep lake whose fish stocks are unaffected by stocking or watercourse regulation. Known for big char, summer and winter, with cloudberry bogs around it.

name: Stordalen (Hávgavuopmi)
summary: A valley of particularly tall, untouched birch forest with a rich ground flora, below the Rohkunborri massif.

name: Jordbruelva
summary: A watercourse whose lakes have never held fish; instead they hold fairy shrimp and tadpole shrimp, food for upland ducks.

name: Eartebealjávri
summary: A lake in the far east of the park, ringed by cloudberry bogs and known for unusually big char.

name: Isdalen
summary: A side valley on the park's north-western edge, one of the places the park brochure singles out for a visit.

name: Lappjordhytta
summary: DNT cabin

name: Rondslottet
summary: Rondane's highest summit at 2,178 metres, reached by a marked path from Rondvassbu over Vinjeronden: about five hours up and three down.

name: Storronden
summary: A 2,138-metre summit on the east side of Rondvatnet, one of the 2,000-metre tops a marked path reaches.

name: Rondvatnet
summary: The long, narrow lake at the heart of the range, walled in by Storronden and the Smiubelgen peaks. Its old name, Rond, became the mountains' name.

name: Smiubelgen
summary: 'The blacksmith's bellows': the jagged massif west of Rondvatnet, with Storsmeden and Veslesmeden among its tops. Officially spelt Smiubelgin.

name: Formokampen
summary: A 1,428-metre top above Høvringen, an hour and a half to two hours on a good path that follows the old reindeer trappers. A family walk with a wide view.

name: Sohlbergplassen
summary: A platform among the pines above Atnsjøen on the National Tourist Route, near one of the spots from which Harald Sohlberg studied Rondane.

name: Straumbu (Strømbu)
summary: Rest area by the Atna and the main entrance from the east, with a roof terrace and toilets. The path to Bjørnhollia takes about two hours.

name: Eldåbu
summary: DNT cabin

name: Rondvassbu
summary: DNT cabin

name: Svabu
summary: Run by Sollia Fjellstyre

name: Vuludalsbua
summary: Run by Sollia Fjellstyre

name: Svartisen
summary: Mainland Norway's second-largest glacier, about 370 square kilometres of ice split in two by Vesterdalen and crossed by the Arctic Circle.

name: Engabreen (Engenbreen)
summary: Svartisen's best-known outlet, down to about 200 metres above sea level; summer boat across Holandsfjorden, then a walk along Engabrevatnet. The lower tongue lies just outside the park.

name: Austerdalsisen
summary: A glacier arm on the Rana side, reached by a summer boat across Svartisvatnet or a rough path along the lake.

name: Marmorslottet
summary: 'The Marble Castle': marble formations in the karst landscape of Glomdalen, one of Saltfjellet's biggest attractions. Its west side lies in the park, its east side in Fisktjønna nature reserve.

name: Bredek
summary: A mountain farm whose buildings are owned by Helgeland Museum and its hay meadows mown again for their flowers. Opened as a visiting farm in summer.

name: Bjøllådalen
summary: A broad valley on the Telegraph Route, with the Krukkimyra bogs — one of the two valleys the Spar Saltfjellet campaign kept from being dammed.

name: Helgelandsbukken
summary: The summit above the Tåkeheimen hut, north of Engabreen; many walkers spend two nights at the hut to climb it.

name: Besøkssenter nasjonalpark Nordland
summary: The authorised visitor centre at Storjord on the E6 in Saltdal, with the exhibition Uerstattelig, maps and route advice for Nordland's national parks.

name: Bjellåvasstua
summary: DNT cabin

name: Blakkådalshytta
summary: DNT cabin

name: Krukkistua
summary: DNT cabin

name: Midtistua
summary: DNT cabin

name: Saltfjellstua
summary: DNT cabin

name: Tåkeheimen
summary: DNT cabin

name: Templet
summary: A 766-metre mountain on the north side of Tempelfjorden, its layered cliffs cut by gullies into the likeness of a ruined cathedral.

name: Tempelfjorden
summary: The innermost arm of Sassenfjorden, between Bünsow Land and Sabine Land, with two glaciers at its head. After 1 March snowmobiles may only cross its ice.

name: Tunabreen
summary: A glacier about 23 kilometres long, flowing from the ice field Lomonosovfonna down to the head of Tempelfjorden.

name: Von Postbreen
summary: About 15 kilometres of glacier ending at the head of Tempelfjorden, named after the Swedish geologist Hampus von Post.

name: Sassendalen
summary: A broad, open valley running south-east and then east from Sassenfjorden to the glacier Rabotbreen.

name: Gipsdalen
summary: An ice-free valley about 22 kilometres long through southern Bünsow Land, named for the gypsum beds in the mountains around it.

name: Brucebyen
summary: Empty houses near Kapp Napier on Billefjorden, named after the Scottish polar explorer William Speirs Bruce; a protected cultural monument.

name: Seilandsjøkelen
summary: The island's largest glacier, lying unusually low, whose meltwater turns the lakes below it milky turquoise.

name: Nordmannsjøkelen
summary: A glacier now split into separate patches, listed on the Global Glacier Casualty List. Crevasses ring part of Seilandstuva.

name: Seilandstuva
summary: Seiland's highest point at 1,078 metres: a long, demanding ascent, usually from Kufjordbotn. Struve's surveyors built its cairn in 1847 for the meridian arc.

name: Melkevatna
summary: A hummocky plateau of glacier-fed lakes south of Seilandsjøkelen, drained by Melkelva. There is no bridge over the river, and fording it is dangerous.

name: Store Bekkarfjord
summary: A fjord of steep, grassy hay slopes with a public floating jetty, a fire site and an artwork telling the haymakers' story. No public transport; several firms run boat trips.

name: Bårdfjorden
summary: An abandoned fjord settlement on the west side; Bårdfjorddalen and Pederdalen offer relatively easy walking.

name: Jøfjorden
summary: A long fjord that almost cuts the island in two; from Breihovddalen above it a route climbs towards Seilandsjøkelen.

name: Sjunkhatten
summary: The park's highest summit at 1,185 metres, a landmark on the west side of Sjunkfjorden that gives the park its name.

name: Sjunkfjorden
summary: A fjord reaching into the heart of the park, where a few families still live from farming and fishing on the old infields.

name: Kvalhornet
summary: One of the classic ski tops of Sjunkhatten, with easy access, reliable snow and a view over the park's fjords and peaks.

name: Finnkonnakken
summary: A popular walk on the Bodø side. Its traffic rose sharply when it joined Bodø's 'ten summits' list, and boardwalks have since been laid over wet ground.

name: Sætervatnet
summary: A lake and wetland in Øvre Valnesfjord where divers, velvet scoter and horned grebe breed; one of the park's most important places for water birds.

name: Steigtinden
summary: A landmark peak on the Bodø side of the park, climbed by groups from Sjunkhatten camp school.

name: Besøkssenter nasjonalpark Nordland
summary: The authorised visitor centre for Sjunkhatten, at Storjord on the E6 in Saltdal, with exhibitions, maps and route advice.

name: Fongen
summary: The park's highest summit at 1,441 metres, rising in the south-east above Schulzhytta and upper Roltdalen.

name: Roltdalen
summary: The largest roadless forest and summer-farm valley in the old county of Sør-Trøndelag, with the park's near-virgin spruce forest.

name: Stormoen
summary: The summer farm beside Schulzhytta, on a slag heap from iron smelting some 2,000 years ago; a mining colony lived here from 1756 to 1810, and dairying went on until 1969.

name: Høgfjellet
summary: Rows of millstone quarries, the densest in the park, crossed by the marked path from Hoemskjølen to Schulzhytta. Explore, but leave every stone.

name: Stor-Kvennfjellvatnet
summary: A mountain lake in the Selbu millstone belt, with many quarries to its north and south.

name: Storskarven
summary: A summit of the Skarvan massif in the north of the park, reached by a marked route from Sildra.

name: Prestøyhytta
summary: DNT cabin

name: Schulzhytta
summary: DNT cabin

name: Lompola
summary: The slow-flowing stretch of the Stabburselva, a chain of winding pools and sedge marsh inside the pine forest — unusually lush this far north.

name: Stabbursfossen
summary: A waterfall on the Stabburselva, 5.5 kilometres from the Lombolaveien car park on a blue-marked path through pine, birch and open plain. Watch for salmon jumping.

name: Stuorra Biŋalvárri
summary: A 528-metre top 7.5 kilometres from the car park on a red-marked path, from pine forest past Lompola to bare mountain, with a view over the valley and Porsangerfjorden.

name: Čohkarášša
summary: The highest of the bare gáisá summits in the middle of the park, standing high above the flat plateaus of Finnmark.

name: Upper Stabburselva
summary: Above Njáhkagorži, where the salmon stop, the river runs on through open plateau; trout are fished here and in the mountain lakes.

name: Stabbursnes Naturhus og Museum
summary: The park's authorised visitor centre, where the Stabburselva meets the fjord: an exhibition and film on Finnmark's nature and culture. Open all year.

name: Hornsund
summary: The southernmost fjord on Spitsbergen's west coast, ringed by sharp peaks and glaciers. Named in 1610 after a reindeer antler.

name: Hornsundtind
summary: About 1,430 metres of crystalline limestone on the south side of Hornsund, at the northern end of Sørkapp Land.

name: Brepollen
summary: The innermost basin of Hornsund, below the glaciers Storbreen, Hornbreen, Svalisbreen and Mendeleevbreen.

name: Burgerbukta
summary: Twin bays on Hornsund's north shore, formed as the glaciers Mühlbacherbreen and Paierlbreen retreated; the western arm opened between 1936 and 1959.

name: Gåshamna
summary: 'The goose bay', an open bay on Hornsund's south shore where a seventeenth-century whaling station has been excavated.

name: Isbjørnhamna
summary: A bay in front of the glacier Hansbreen, near the mouth of Hornsund, where Poland has kept a research station since 1957.

name: Sørkapp
summary: Spitsbergen's south cape, the tip of the island Sørkappøya. A bird reserve, closed to all traffic from 15 May to 15 August.

name: Reindalen
summary: The largest ice-free valley on Spitsbergen, about 38 kilometres long, opening onto the wet delta plain of Stormyra and the bay of Kaldbukta.

name: Stormyra
summary: A wet plain about seven kilometres across at the mouth of Reindalen, where several rivers braid their way to the bay of Kaldbukta.

name: Ingeborgfjellet
summary: A 714-metre mountain on the Bellsund coast whose cliffs hold colonies of little auks, Brünnich's guillemots and kittiwakes.

name: Fridtjovhamna
summary: A bay on the outer north shore of Van Mijenfjorden, left behind as the glacier Fridtjovbreen retreated; key ground for ice-dependent animals.

name: Akseløya
summary: An island 8.5 kilometres long and about a kilometre wide that lies across the mouth of Van Mijenfjorden, leaving only narrow sounds on either side.

name: Midterhuken
summary: The mountain headland between Bellsund's two arms, Van Mijenfjorden and Van Keulenfjorden. Marked areas on it are closed to all traffic from 15 May to 15 August.

name: Rindersbukta
summary: The southern inner arm of Van Mijenfjorden, below the glaciers Scheelebreen and Paulabreen; named after the Dutch whaling skipper Michiel Rinders.

name: Skipskjølen
summary: The park's highest point at 633 metres, on the low ridge that forms the peninsula's watershed: blockfields and ring moraines from before the last ice age.

name: Komagdalen (Stuorrajohka)
summary: A valley with a 4-kilometre marked bird trail from the car park; a suspension bridge leads on towards Bjørneskarhytta, 18 kilometres in.

name: Nattfjelldalen (Idjaávži)
summary: A meltwater gorge in the plateau, four kilometres by car from Vadsø. The marked path ends at the park boundary; the rim route is nine kilometres one way.

name: Sandfjorddalen
summary: One of the park's most distinctive valleys, green and lush, with salmon and sea char in Sandfjordelva.

name: Oarddojávri (Ordo)
summary: A lake on the park's edge with good fishing, where Syltefjordelva begins; the usual start for the open hut Helheim, seven kilometres away as the crow flies.

name: Kjøpmannskjølen
summary: Site of Noidiidcearru, the best known of the stone fences and trapping systems built to catch wild reindeer.

name: Bjørneskarhytta
summary: Run by Varangerhalvøya nasjonalpark

name: Heimdal
summary: Run by Båtsfjord Røde Kors

name: Helheim
summary: Run by Båtsfjord Røde Kors

name: Ragnarokk
summary: Run by Båtsfjord Røde Kors

name: Tisler and the Tisler reef
summary: An outer island above one of the world's largest inshore cold-water coral reefs: Lophelia growing 74 to 160 metres down, 1,200 metres long.

name: Søsterøyene
summary: The Sister Islands off Fredrikstad, built of rhomb-porphyry conglomerate, a rock found in few places on Earth. Seabird zones close parts of them in spring.

name: Akerøya
summary: A seabird island with a bird-ringing station. Parts of it are closed from 15 April to 15 July, and camping there is banned all year.

name: Torbjørnskjær lighthouse
summary: A granite lighthouse of 1872 on a skerry marking the east side of the entrance to the Oslofjord, automated since 1990 and now protected.

name: Vesterøy coast path
summary: Six kilometres of the blue-marked Kyststien along the shore from Papperhavn past Kuvauen and Guttormsvauen to Utgård.

name: Storesand
summary: A beach near Skjærhalden with tent pitches, where the visitor centre runs sessions exploring the shoreline.

name: Besøkssenter Ytre Hvaler nasjonalpark
summary: The authorised visitor centre in the old granary, Kornmagasinet, at Skjærhalden, with an exhibition, maps, guided trips and summer tourist information.

name: Åndervatnet
summary: The lake at the heart of the park, its islets moraine mounds left by stagnant ice. A boardwalked path leads in from Tranøybotn to a lakeside rest area.

name: Kvænan
summary: The park's highest summit at 964 metres, and the second highest on Senja: a sharp outer-coast peak and a popular ski-touring top in winter.

name: Istinden
summary: An 851-metre peak marking the park's northern edge, where the Senja på langs route climbs in from Kaperdalen. A favourite ski-touring top.

name: Kolkjerka
summary: A prominent 745-metre summit rising from the middle of the park.

name: Kapervatnet
summary: A lake north of Åndervatnet, lined with moraine hummocks and big boulders, on the river that comes down from Kaperfjellet through a deep, narrow gorge.

name: Trolldalen
summary: A long, narrow side valley with tall birch forest that has been left largely alone.

name: Ånderelva
summary: The river that runs in falls and rapids from Åndervatnet to the sea at Tranøybotn; salmon, sea trout and sea char run its lower reaches.

name: Sážžá Senja naturhus & museum
summary: The park board's base at Øverbotn, shared with Midt-Troms Museum: a permanent exhibition on Senja's nature and culture centred on Ånderdalen, open in summer. Check opening times before you go.

name: Kjerringhøgda fire tower
summary: A fire lookout with views over much of the park, on a site first used for a tower probably in the late 1800s. A short round walk from Bysetermåsan.

name: Tonekollen
summary: One of Østmarka's highest tops: a demanding climb to a summit with wide views, especially towards Øyeren and Lillestrøm.

name: Mosjøen
summary: A long lake in the heart of the park. Canoes can be hired at Vangen skistue on its western side.

name: Svartoren
summary: A narrow lake almost three kilometres long between rocky, wooded banks — good paddling close to the forest.

name: Spinneren
summary: A long ridge of old pine forest and intact wild country close to the city, protected in 2013 and now partly inside the park.

name: Rausjøgrenda
summary: A hamlet of old sawmill buildings on the park's edge, a living memorial of the timber trade. The historic plank road, Plankeveien, runs through it.

name: Bysetermåsan
summary: The main southern gateway, with a car park, information about the park and paths, roads and ski trails into its heart.

name: Bøvelstad
summary: DNT cabin

name: Skaktardalen
summary: An impressive canyon cut into the valley side, about an hour's walk from the road in Dividalen.

name: Skaktaråsen
summary: A short climb from the Skaktermoen car park to a view over the high country towards the Swedish border. A culture and nature trail nearby suits children.

name: Øvre Divifoss
summary: A waterfall on the Divielva just outside the park boundary, with potholes worn deep into the rock beside it.

name: Jerta
summary: A 1,428-metre summit in the east of the park. A red granite boulder carried from Sweden by the ice sits beside the summit cairn.

name: Anjavassdalen
summary: The park's western valley, around the lake Anjavatnet and the Anja river.

name: Čievččasjávri
summary: Lake where the Swedish Sámi community of Lainiovuoma has its summer settlement; about 200 people gather here in early July for calf marking.

name: Hávgavuopmi
summary: A forested area in the south-east of the park, the one part where all hunting and trapping is banned.

name: Anjavasshytta
summary: Run by Statskog

name: Dividalshytta
summary: DNT cabin

name: Dærtahytta
summary: DNT cabin

name: Ole Nergårdbua
summary: Run by Statskog

name: Vuomahytta
summary: DNT cabin

name: Treriksrøysa
summary: The cairn on Krokfjellet where Norway, Finland and Russia meet, about 5 km by path from Grensefoss. You may not walk round it or climb it.

name: Ellenvatnet
summary: The park's largest lake, in its centre. A marked path from Sortbrysttjern leads to the open cabin Ellenvannskoia.

name: Ødevatnet
summary: A long, narrow lake lying in a deep fault in the bedrock; the same fault runs on north-east to the cliffs of Revsaksskaret.

name: Revsaksskaret
summary: Steep cliffs in the south-east of the park, on the fault line that runs north-east from Ødevatnet.

name: Sortbrysttjern
summary: Trailhead with parking, a shelter, fire site and toilet. The path to Ellenvannskoia carries boards on nature and Sámi culture, and continues into Finland's Vätsäri wilderness.

name: Grensefoss
summary: Trailhead for Treriksrøysa, with parking, a shelter, fire site and toilet; the path runs about 5 km to the cairn.

name: Besøkssenter Øvre Pasvik nasjonalpark (NIBIO Svanhovd)
summary: The park's authorised visitor centre at Svanvik: exhibitions on the forest, the brown bear and the Skolt Sámi, a botanical garden, and rooms to stay.

name: Tongariro Alpine Crossing
summary: A 20-kilometre one-way walk from Mangatepōpō over Red Crater, at 1,886 metres the highest point, down to Ketetahi Road. Seven to eight hours in summer.

name: Ngā Rotopounamu / Emerald Lakes
summary: Old explosion pits below Red Crater, coloured by minerals washed down from its thermal area. Sacred lakes: do not touch or enter the water.

name: Te Wai Whakaata o Te Rangihīroa / Blue Lake
summary: Rangihīroa's mirror: cold fresh water filling an old vent beside the Alpine Crossing, across Central Crater from Red Crater.

name: Ngāuruhoe
summary: The symmetrical young cone of the Tongariro complex, about 7,000 years old. Its summit is sacred; enjoy it from the Crossing and the Northern Circuit.

name: Ruapehu
summary: The North Island's highest mountain, 2,797 metres, with glaciers, the Whakapapa and Tūroa ski areas, and Te Wai ā-moe/Crater Lake in its active vent.

name: Taranaki Falls
summary: A waterfall plunging into a boulder-ringed pool, on one of the park's best short loop walks from Whakapapa Village; each half of the loop takes about an hour.

name: Tama Lakes
summary: Two infilled explosion craters on Tama Saddle between Ruapehu and Ngāuruhoe, named after Tamatea, high chief of the Takitimu canoe. The upper lake is a steep climb further.

name: Ohinepango Springs
summary: Clear, cold water bubbling up from beneath an old lava flow, an hour's return side trip from Waihohonu Hut.

name: Lake Rotopounamu
summary: A forest-ringed lake beneath Pihanga, in the Pihanga Scenic Reserve, the detached northern part of the park near Tūrangi.

name: Tongariro National Park Visitor Centre
summary: DOC's visitor centre in Whakapapa Village, for track conditions, volcanic and avalanche advice and Alpine Crossing bookings.

name: Taranaki Maunga
summary: The 2,518-metre summit, a demanding climb of 1.6 vertical kilometres from North Egmont, best attempted January to April. Ice lies in the crater all year.

name: Pouākai tarns
summary: Small alpine pools on the Pouākai Range where, on a fine day, the mountain is mirrored. Keep to the boardwalk and do not enter the pools.

name: Ahukawakawa
summary: An alpine swamp between the mountain and the Pouākai Range, home to a third of the park's plant species, crossed on a boardwalk.

name: Te Rere-o-Tahurangi Falls
summary: A 31-metre waterfall where the Hangatahua River has cut through an ancient lava flow; an hour's return side trip from Holly Hut.

name: Dawson Falls / Te Rere o Noke
summary: An 18-metre waterfall near the Dawson Falls road end, on the mountain's south-eastern side.

name: Wilkies Pools
summary: Pools scoured from 20,000-year-old lava, reached through goblin forest in 20 minutes from Dawson Falls; the first 900 metres suit buggies and wheelchairs.

name: Panitahi
summary: The secondary vent on the mountain's southern flank, formed where magma found a weak point in the volcano; the Around the Mountain Circuit passes below it.

name: Dawson Falls Power Station
summary: Installed in 1935 to power the tourist lodge; its generator is the oldest in continuous operation in New Zealand. View the machine room from outside.

name: North Taranaki Visitor Centre
summary: DOC visitor centre at the top of Egmont Road, start of the summit climb and Pouākai Crossing. A new centre is being built; check opening hours.

name: Dawson Falls Visitor Centre
summary: A small visitor centre at the end of Manaia Road, with displays that include the old Syme Hut rebuilt inside.

name: Bridge to Nowhere
summary: A concrete bridge nearly 40 metres above the Mangapurua Stream, opened in 1936 for a soldier settlement that had already failed. A 40-minute walk from Mangapurua Landing.

name: Mangapurua Landing
summary: The river landing for the Bridge to Nowhere, reached by canoe or jet boat. The rock is very slippery when wet and often crowded with boats.

name: Whanganui Journey
summary: The Great Walk by canoe: 88 kilometres from Whakahoro to Pipiriki in about three days, through the most scenic gorges, or 145 kilometres from Taumarunui in five.

name: Matemateāonga Track
summary: A 42-kilometre tramp of three to five days along an old Māori trail and settlers' dray road on the crest of the Matemateāonga Range, ending at the river.

name: Whakaihuwaka Maunga
summary: A 732-metre summit off the Matemateāonga Track with a view of three national parks: Whanganui, Te Papa-Kura-o-Taranaki and Tongariro.

name: Atene Skyline Track
summary: A 12.5-kilometre ridge walk from the Whanganui River Road around Puketapu hill and a cut-off meander of the river, rising to 572 metres at Taumata Trig.

name: Cascade Falls
summary: A waterfall hidden in native bush, a steep 1 hour 30 minute return side trip on the Coast Track section from Anchorage to Bark Bay.

name: Falls River suspension bridge
summary: A 47-metre suspension bridge over the inlet of Falls River, between Torrent Bay and Bark Bay.

name: Onetahuti Bay
summary: One of the longest beaches in the park, reached after a climb through mānuka from Bark Bay and the old granite workings at Tonga Quarry.

name: Tonga Island
summary: A specially protected island where fur seals breed, off Onetahuti Bay. Landing needs a permit.

name: Awaroa Inlet
summary: A wide sandy estuary on the Coast Track that can be crossed only in daylight, from 1 hour 30 minutes before to 2 hours after low tide.

name: Tōtaranui
summary: A beach and campsite at the northern end of the water-taxi service, with the historic Ngarata homestead; farmed until 1974.

name: Separation Point / Te Matau
summary: The granite headland at the park's northern tip, where fur seals rest on the rocks and bryozoans build coral-like colonies under water.

name: Motuareronui / Adele Island
summary: An island free of introduced mammal predators. Land by boat or kayak, check your gear for stowaway pests, and take everything away again.

name: Lake Rotoiti and Kerr Bay
summary: The glacial lake at St Arnaud, ringed by beech forest, with a campsite, boat ramp, lakeshore walks and the bird-filled Rotoiti Nature Recovery Project.

name: Lake Rotoroa
summary: The 'long lake', reached by a side road between St Arnaud and Murchison; a water taxi links Rotoroa village with Sabine Hut.

name: Mount Robert
summary: The peak above Lake Rotoiti; from Mount Robert car park the Pinchgut Track and the Robert Ridge route lead to Lake Angelus.

name: Rotomaninitua / Lake Angelus
summary: An alpine lake at 1,650 metres in the Travers Range, with Angelus Hut on its shore. Frozen in most winters, May to October.

name: Whisky Falls
summary: A waterfall a short diversion off the Lakeside Track on the western shore of Lake Rotoiti, on the way to Coldwater Hut.

name: Travers Falls
summary: A 20-metre cascade plunging into a deep bowl, a short side track above John Tait Hut on the Travers–Sabine Circuit.

name: Poukirikiri / Travers Saddle
summary: The circuit's alpine pass, 450 metres above Upper Travers Hut, with panoramic views and a steep 1,000-metre descent to the Sabine forks. Freezing conditions possible all year.

name: Rotomairewhenua / Blue Lake
summary: Thought to be the clearest natural freshwater lake in the world, an overnight side trip up the West Sabine. Tapu: do not touch the water.

name: Pancake Rocks and Blowholes
summary: Layered limestone stacks, surge pools and blowholes at Dolomite Point, on a 30-minute paved loop mostly suitable for wheelchairs. Best at high tide with a south-westerly swell.

name: Truman Track
summary: A 30-minute return walk from the highway north of Punakaiki through nīkau forest and flax to platforms above a wild beach and a waterfall off sandstone cliffs.

name: Pororari River gorge
summary: A limestone gorge with huge boulders and deep pools, a lookout 15 minutes from the road, and the walkers' entry to the Paparoa Track. Rockfall: don't linger in the gorge.

name: Ballroom Overhang
summary: A huge limestone overhang up the Fox River, with a toilet and room to camp. A demanding 4-hour return with unbridged river crossings; avoid after rain.

name: Pike29 Memorial Track
summary: Climbs about 800 metres from the former Pike River mine site to the Paparoa Track, with views of the mine's vent shaft; dedicated to the 29 men killed in 2010.

name: Paparoa National Park Visitor Centre
summary: DOC visitor centre on the Coast Road at Punakaiki, for the latest track and river conditions.

name: Devils Punchbowl Falls/Te Tautea o Hinekakai
summary: A 131-metre waterfall at the north end of the village, reached by 400-plus steps through mountain beech to a platform at its base; about an hour return.

name: Avalanche Peak
summary: At 1,833 metres, the only peak in the park with a marked route to the top: 1,100 metres of climbing from the village. People have died on it.

name: Arthur's Pass and the Dobson Nature Walk
summary: The summit of the pass on SH73. A short walk from the Temple Basin car park passes alpine plants, including the Mt Cook buttercup, which flower from November to February.

name: Ōtira Viaduct
summary: The highway's bridge across the slips and rockfall of the Ōtira Gorge on the West Coast side, built between 1998 and 1999.

name: Otira Valley Track
summary: A graded track under the north flank of Mount Rolleston/Kaimatau to the Otira River footbridge, with summer alpine flowers. Avalanches cross it from May to November.

name: Bealey Spur
summary: A gentle climb through mountain beech and tussock past tarns, with wide views of the Waimakariri valley. Often drier than the village when north-westerlies bring rain.

name: Goat Pass
summary: The crossing of the main divide on the two-to-three-day Mingha–Deception route, part of Te Araroa and of the Coast to Coast race. For experienced, well-equipped trampers only.

name: Mount Rolleston/Kaimatau
summary: The glacier-hung massif that dominates the view west of the pass, seen from the Avalanche Peak route and the Otira Valley. A climb for mountaineers.

name: Arthur's Pass National Park Visitor Centre
summary: DOC's visitor centre at 104 West Coast Road, for track conditions, the avalanche advisory and the weather forecast before you set out.

name: Franz Josef Glacier/Kā Roimata o Hine Hukatere
summary: A 30-minute return walk through rainforest to a view up the glacier valley. The Waiho River has cut off access further up; never go past the barriers.

name: Sentinel Rock
summary: A glacier-smoothed schist knoll in the Franz Josef valley, with views of the glacier, the valley and the Waiho River. Ice pressed against nearby Harper Rock until 1909.

name: Roberts Point
summary: A challenging 12.3-kilometre return hike past historic Hende's Gallery to a lookout high above the Franz Josef ice. Unbridged creeks and slippery slabs; choose a dry day.

name: Alex Knob
summary: An eight-hour return climb from rainforest to alpine meadows, with what DOC calls the best views of Franz Josef Glacier without a helicopter. Start early to beat the afternoon cloud.

name: Fox Glacier/Te Moeka o Tuawe
summary: The South Side Walkway follows the Fox River through podocarp forest to a glacier viewpoint, 6.4 km return. The glacier is the moeka, final resting place, of Tuawe.

name: Lake Matheson/Te Ara Kairaumati
summary: A glacier-formed lake whose dark water mirrors Aoraki/Mount Cook and Mount Tasman/Te Horokōau on calm days. A 4.4-km loop; the first section to Jetty Lookout suits wheelchairs.

name: Ōkārito Lagoon
summary: A wide coastal lagoon on the park's northern edge, famous for the kōtuku/white heron; the old gold-rush settlement of Ōkārito stands beside it.

name: Lake Māpōurika
summary: A lake north of Franz Josef/Waiau, home to the threatened kāmana/crested grebe.

name: Welcome Flat hot pools
summary: Natural hot pools by Welcome Flat Hut, seven hours up the Copland Track, facing the Sierra Range. No soap, no digging; keep your head above water.

name: Westland Tai Poutini National Park Visitor Centre
summary: DOC's visitor centre at 69 Cron Street, Franz Josef/Waiau, for weather, track conditions and the region's history; the historic Cape Defiance Hut is on display here.

name: Aoraki/Mount Cook
summary: New Zealand's highest mountain at 3,724 metres, sacred to Ngāi Tahu as their most revered ancestor. Seen from the Hooker Valley Track, Kea Point and Tasman Glacier View.

name: Hooker Valley Track
summary: Ten kilometres return from White Horse Hill to Hooker Lake at the foot of Aoraki, over three swing bridges, one the country's longest at 189 m. Icebergs in summer.

name: Tasman Glacier View and the Blue Lakes
summary: Over 300 steps up a moraine wall to a view across Tasman Lake to Haupapa/Tasman Glacier; a side track reaches the first Blue Lake, now green with rainwater.

name: Haupapa/Tasman Glacier
summary: New Zealand's largest and longest glacier, 23 km long and up to 3 km wide, its lower reaches covered in rock. Visible from the highway at the park entrance.

name: Kea Point
summary: A gentle walk across subalpine grassland to a deck on the Mueller Glacier moraine wall, facing Mount Sefton, the Hooker Valley and Aoraki. Two hours return from the village.

name: Sealy Tarns
summary: The 'stairway to heaven': 2,200 steps and 600 metres of climbing to small alpine lakes above the Hooker Valley. No shelter; turn back if north-west weather approaches.

name: Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park Visitor Centre
summary: DOC's visitor centre at 1 Larch Grove in the village, with exhibits, an art collection, and advice on huts, weather and avalanche conditions.

name: Mount Aspiring/Tititea
summary: The park's namesake, the only peak over 3,000 metres outside Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park; its Māori name means the steep peak of glistening white. A mountaineer's summit.

name: Rob Roy Track
summary: Ten kilometres return from Raspberry Creek, over a swing bridge and up through beech forest to views of Rob Roy Glacier. From May to November, stop at the lower lookout.

name: Cascade Saddle
summary: An exposed alpine crossing from the West Matukituki to the Dart, best in mid to late summer and only for experienced, well-equipped trampers. Multiple people have died on it.

name: Blue Pools
summary: Snow-fed pools in the Makarora River, clear and blue after dry weather; an easy 1.5-hour return walk through silver beech and over two swing bridges. No jumping off them.

name: Haast Pass/Tioripatea Lookout
summary: A one-hour return climb of 150 metres from the top of the pass to a viewpoint above the beech forest, with Mount Brewster prominent to the north-east.

name: Gillespie Pass
summary: The high point of a 56-km, three-to-four-day circuit through the Young and Wilkin valleys, with a side trip to Crucible Lake. For experienced parties with river-crossing skills.

name: Routeburn Falls
summary: The cascade at the bushline above the Routeburn Flats, two and a half to four hours up the Routeburn Track from the Routeburn Shelter, below the climb to Harris Saddle.

name: Wānaka Tititea/Mount Aspiring National Park Visitor Centre
summary: DOC's visitor centre in Wānaka, for weather, track and road conditions and hut bookings before heading into the park.

name: Milford Sound/Piopiotahi
summary: The fiord at the end of the Milford Road, 16 km long and up to 265 m deep. Cruises leave from the visitor terminal; a marine reserve protects its waters.

name: Mitre Peak
summary: Sheer rock walls rising 1,692 metres straight from the water, one of the world's most photographed peaks. The Milford Sound Foreshore Walk has some of the best views.

name: Sutherland Falls
summary: Falls dropping 580 metres in three leaps from Lake Quill, a side trip of 1 hr 30 min return on the third day of the Milford Track, below Omanui/McKinnon Pass.

name: Mirror Lakes
summary: Small lakes beside the Milford Road, about 56 km from Te Anau, reflecting the Earl Mountains. A 10-minute wheelchair-accessible stroll.

name: Key Summit
summary: A side trip from the Routeburn Track near The Divide to an alpine wetland, with views of the Darran Mountains and Hollyford Valley; 1–1.5 hours return.

name: Lake Marian
summary: An alpine lake in a glacier-carved hanging valley, 1.5 hours up a steep track off Hollyford Road; waterfalls 10 minutes in. Keep off the lake edge in winter and spring.

name: Homer Tunnel
summary: The Milford Road's tunnel, begun in 1935 and finished in 1954. Traffic signals can hold you up to 20 minutes; kea are often seen here.

name: Doubtful Sound/Patea
summary: A large, remote fiord with three main arms and no road, home to one of the southernmost bottlenose dolphin populations. Reached by boat and coach via Lake Manapōuri.

name: Mount Luxmore
summary: The highest point of the Kepler Track at 1,472 metres, a 30-minute side trip from the ridge, with views over Lake Te Anau's South Fiord to the Murchison Mountains.

name: Lake Hauroko
summary: New Zealand's deepest lake, 462 metres, in the south of the park, reached by road off the Southern Scenic Route; boats can be launched here.

name: Te Rua-o-te-moko/Fiordland National Park Visitor Centre
summary: DOC's visitor centre at 1 Lakefront Drive, Te Anau, for Great Walk bookings, track and road conditions, hunting and boating advice.

name: Lee Bay
summary: The official entrance to the park, 5 km from Oban, where the Rakiura Track passes through a chain-link sculpture recalling the island as the anchor of Māui's canoe.

name: Māori Beach
summary: A Rakiura Track beach that was a sawmilling settlement, with a school, until the 1930s; a boiler and steam engine remain. A 6–7 hour return day walk from Oban.

name: Garden Mound
summary: A steep, muddy climb to 160 metres through unmilled rimu, rātā, miro and kāmahi, with views over Oban; return by the coast via Lee Bay. Four to five hours.

name: Ulva Island/Te Wharawhara
summary: A predator-free open sanctuary in Paterson Inlet, a short boat ride from Halfmoon Bay or Golden Bay, where saddleback, mohua and kiwi thrive. Day visits only.

name: Mason Bay
summary: A long west-coast beach backed by great dunes, on the North West and Southern circuits. Its northern end can be passed only at low tide; check tide times with DOC.

name: Mount Anglem/Hananui
summary: The island's highest point, 980 metres: a six-hour return side trip from Christmas Village Hut on the North West Circuit, through forest and leatherwood. Often muddy and foggy.

name: Rakiura National Park Visitor Centre
summary: DOC's visitor centre at 15 Main Road, Oban, for track and weather updates, Mason Bay tide times, hut passes and hunting permits.
